definition_zh: 季度的；按季度的；每季度地；季刊
definition_en: happening or produced once every three months, or a magazine published four times a year
core_image: 一年被一刀切成四块，每到一块交界处就结一次账、出一期刊
scene: 财务部的墙上挂着日历，每到一块边界就圈出一次汇报。The finance team files a quarterly report before the board meets each spring, summer, autumn and winter.
sceneCN: 这里 quarterly 是「季度的」（第 1 个义项：每三个月发生一次的）；句意：董事会春夏秋冬每次开会之前，财务团队都会提交一份季度报告。

pos.zh: 季度的；按季度的；一年四次的

derivatives.zh: 基础词：四分之一，一年的四分之一就是「季度」
同根名词：四分之一加仑，来自拉丁语「四分之一」

senses.title: Happening once every three months
senses.titleCN: 季度的；每三个月一次的
senses.definition: happening, produced, or paid once in every three months
senses.definitionCN: 每三个月发生、产生或支付一次的
senses.example: The company publishes a quarterly report on its sales.
senses.exampleCN: 公司按季度发布销售报告。
senses.why: One year splits into four quarters, and the suffix -ly turns the unit into a repeating rhythm, so quarterly means that rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 一年被分成四个季度，后缀 -ly 把这个单位变成一种循环节奏，所以 quarterly 表示按这种节奏重复。

senses.title: At intervals of three months
senses.definition: in a way that happens at the end of every three-month period
senses.definitionCN: 以每三个月一次的方式；按季度地
senses.example: The accounts are reviewed quarterly by an outside auditor.
senses.exampleCN: 账目每季度由外部审计师审查一次。
senses.why: The same -ly form works as an adverb of time, telling not what kind of thing it is but how often things are done.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ly 形式可作时间副词，说明的不是事物性质，而是事情多久做一次。

senses.title: A magazine issued four times a year
senses.definition: a magazine or journal that appears four times a year
senses.definitionCN: 每年出版四次的杂志或期刊
senses.example: Her short story appeared in a small literary quarterly.
senses.exampleCN: 她的短篇小说发表在一本小型文学季刊上。
senses.why: English often turns frequency adjectives into nouns for periodicals, so a quarterly is simply a publication that keeps the quarterly rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把表频率的形容词转成名词指定期刊物，所以 quarterly 就是保持季度节奏出版的刊物。

senses.title: Describing a quarter as one part of four
senses.titleCN: 由四分之一构成地；以四分之一为单位
senses.definition: in a way that relates to one of four equal parts or to a quarter of a total
senses.definitionCN: 与四个等份之一或以总量的四分之一有关的
senses.example: The old farm was divided quarterly among the four heirs.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老农场被分成四份分给四位继承人。
senses.why: Before it meant every three months, the base word quarter already meant a fourth part, and this rarer use keeps that arithmetic picture.
senses.whyCN: 在表示每三个月之前，基础词 quarter 本义就是「四分之一」，这个较少见的用法保留了那种算术画面。

senses.title: Recurring in the rhythm of the calendar
senses.titleCN: 随季度出现的；季度的周期性
senses.definition: belonging to a repeated pattern that follows the four seasons of the business year
senses.definitionCN: 属于随营业年度四季循环出现的重复模式的
senses.example: Retail sales show a strong quarterly pattern around every holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 零售额在每逢假日的季度都呈现出明显的周期性。
senses.why: Because quarters are fixed calendar blocks, quarterly also describes the regular wave of activity that follows them.
senses.whyCN: 因为季度是固定的日历块，quarterly 也用来描述随这些块起伏的规律性活动。

intro.en: Quarterly is built in English from quarter plus the suffix -ly; quarter itself comes from Latin quartarius, a fourth part.
intro.cn: quarterly 是在英语中由 quarter 加后缀 -ly 构成的；quarter 本身来自拉丁语 quartarius，意为「四分之一」。

items.en: Quartarius means a fourth part, from quartus, the fourth.
items.cn: quartarius 意为四分之一，源于 quartus（第四）。

items.en: Quartier means a fourth part or a district of a town.
items.cn: quartier 意为四分之一或城市的街区。

items.en: Quarter enters English with the sense of a fourth part.
items.cn: quarter 进入英语，表示「四分之一」。

items.en: Quarter grows a time sense: one of the four parts of the year.
items.cn: quarter 发展出时间义：一年四个部分之一。

items.en: Quarterly appears as an adverb and adjective of frequency.
items.cn: quarterly 作为表频率的副词与形容词出现。

items.en: The noun a quarterly names a magazine that comes out four times a year.
items.cn: 名词用法 quarterly 指每年出版四次的期刊。

note.en: Quarterly belongs to the family of frequency words built on calendar units, and shares its base with quarter and quart.
note.cn: quarterly 属于以日历单位为底构成的频率词族，并与 quarter、quart 共享词基。

entries.definition: a fourth part, or a period of three months
a unit equal to a quarter of a gallon
a group of four performers or a piece for four players
happening or published once a month
happening once every year
a magazine that is published at regular intervals

normalIntro.en: Quarterly is calendar arithmetic: a year into four, and the -ly suffix makes the beat repeat.
normalIntro.cn: quarterly 是日历上的算术：一年分成四份，后缀 -ly 让这个节拍循环起来。

normal.en: The word is quarter plus -ly, and quarter means a fourth part.
normal.cn: 这个词是 quarter 加 -ly，而 quarter 意为四分之一。

normal.en: A quarterly report comes out four times a year.
normal.cn: quarterly report 即季度报告，一年出四份。

normal.en: On a quarterly basis means the same as every three months.
normal.cn: on a quarterly basis 与「每三个月一次」同义。

normal.en: Compare the -ly family: monthly, weekly, daily and yearly all mark a repeated rhythm.
normal.cn: 对比 -ly 词族：monthly、weekly、daily、yearly 都表示一种重复的节奏。

normal.en: A quarterly is a magazine with four issues a year, just like a monthly has twelve.
normal.cn: a quarterly 是一年出四期的杂志，正如 monthly 一年出十二期。

abstract.en: Picture a year cut into four cake slices, each with a stamp on its edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一年被切成四块蛋糕，每块边上都盖一个章。

abstract.en: Imagine four cash boxes lined up, one opened at the end of each season.
abstract.cn: 想象四个钱箱排成一列，每季结束时打开其中一个。

abstract.en: Think of a library shelf holding four thin magazines waiting behind one cover.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上一本厚封面后面排队等着四本薄薄的杂志。

examples.en: The firm holds a quarterly meeting to check its progress.
examples.cn: 公司每季度开一次会检查进展。

examples.en: They pay for the security service quarterly.
examples.cn: 他们按季度支付安保服务的费用。

examples.en: The editor of a small quarterly asked her for a review.
examples.cn: 一家小型季刊的编辑向她约了一篇书评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阔特利」——发音像「阔」，一年阔气地切成四块，每块都查一次账；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 quartus（第四）→ quartarius（四分之一）→ 古法语 quartier（四分之一；街区）→ 英语 quarter（四分之一；季度）→ 加后缀 -ly 成 quarterly，核心义「按四份之一的时间节奏重复」。

sensesIntro.en: Quarterly starts from cutting a year into four, then repeats a time rhythm as an adjective, an adverb, and finally names a magazine that follows that rhythm.
sensesIntro.cn: quarterly 从把一年切成四份出发，先作形容词表示时间节奏，再作副词表示按季进行，最后作名词指遵循这种节奏的刊物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a year sliced into four parts, each cut marked by a bill and a new issue.
core.cn: 核心意象：一年被切成四份，每个切口都记一次账、出一期刊。

branches.en: Once in three months is the adjective of frequency.
branches.cn: 每三个月一次是表频率的形容词义。

branches.en: How often a thing is done is the adverb use.
branches.cn: 说明多久做一次是副词用法。

branches.en: A magazine on that rhythm becomes the noun use.
branches.cn: 按这种节奏出版的刊物成为名词用法。

branches.en: The arithmetic sense of a fourth part survives from the base word.
branches.cn: 四分之一这个算术义从基础词保留下来。

branches.en: Fixed calendar blocks create the seasonal pattern the adjective also names.
branches.cn: 固定的日历块造出形容词也用来指称的季节性模式。

intro.en: Quarterly is a native English compound of a noun stem and the suffix -ly, with quarter and quart in the same family.
intro.cn: quarterly 是英语本土构词：名词词干加后缀 -ly，同族词包括 quarter 与 quart。

latinIntro.en: Latin quartus means fourth, and quartarius means a fourth part.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quartus 意为第四，quartarius 意为四分之一。

items.example: Quart keeps the plain fourth-part sense.
items.exampleCN: quart 保留直白的四分之一含义。

items.meaning: a fourth part or a three-month period
items.example: Quarter supplies the calendar unit.
items.exampleCN: quarter 提供日历单位。

items.meaning: in the manner of, happening each
items.example: The suffix -ly turns a unit into a frequency word.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把单位词变成表频率的词。

items.example: Quarterly is the unit plus the frequency suffix.
items.exampleCN: quarterly 是单位词加频率后缀。

items.example: Quartet shares the Latin four.
items.exampleCN: quartet 共享拉丁语「四」。

items.example: Monthly follows the same pattern as quarterly.
items.exampleCN: monthly 与 quarterly 构词方式一致。

items.example: Yearly is another member of the -ly family.
items.exampleCN: yearly 是 -ly 词族的另一个成员。

items.example: Weekly shows the same calendar logic.
items.exampleCN: weekly 体现同样的日历逻辑。

items.meaning: the player who directs the attack
items.example: Quarterback takes quarter from position, not time.
items.exampleCN: quarterback 中的 quarter 来自位置，不是时间。

items.meaning: the main office of an organization
items.example: Headquarters keeps the older sense of a lodging place.
items.exampleCN: headquarters 保留「驻地」的旧义。

definition_zh: 镇压；平息；压制；消除
definition_en: to end or stop something by force, or to calm a strong feeling such as fear or anger
core_image: 一只手掌按在翻腾的沸水上，硬生生把它压到平静
scene: 城市的街道上人群越聚越多，警方被紧急调去压住局面。Riot police were sent in to quell the unrest before it spread to the next district.
sceneCN: 这里 quell 是「镇压、平息」（第 1 个义项：用武力压住暴乱与动乱）；句意：防暴警察被调去平息骚乱，以免事态蔓延到下一个街区。

derivatives.zh: quell 加 -er 构成的施动名词，指镇压者、平息者
动名词形式，指平息或镇压这一动作
un- 加过去分词构成，指未被平息的、仍在持续的抗争

senses.title: To put down a violent disturbance
senses.definition: to end a riot, rebellion, or violent unrest by force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力结束骚乱、叛乱或暴力动乱
senses.example: Soldiers were ordered to quell the riot in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵奉命镇压首都的骚乱。
senses.why: The oldest English sense is killing, and from stopping life the word slid to stopping any violent rising, so a crowd in revolt is put down.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最古老的义项是「杀死」，从终止生命滑向终止任何激烈的反抗，于是暴动的人群就被压平了。

senses.title: To calm a strong feeling
senses.definition: to reduce or get rid of a feeling such as fear, anger, or doubt
senses.definitionCN: 减轻或消除恐惧、愤怒、疑虑等强烈情绪
senses.example: The doctors quelled her fear with a clear explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用清楚的解释消除了她的恐惧。
senses.why: If a riot can be put down, so can an inner uprising, so the same verb lowers the heat of emotion.
senses.whyCN: 既然外部的骚乱能被压下去，心里的「叛乱」也一样，于是同一个动词用来给情绪降温。

senses.title: To suppress openly expressed opposition
senses.definition: to silence or weaken protest, criticism, or resistance
senses.definitionCN: 让抗议、批评或抵抗沉默或变弱
senses.example: The new rules were designed to quell criticism from local groups.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定意在压制当地团体的批评。
senses.why: Opposition has a political side, so the word often implies force or pressure rather than simply answering a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 反对带有政治色彩，所以这个词常隐含使用武力或压力，而不只是回应一下抱怨。

senses.title: To put an end to a physical struggle
senses.definition: to bring a fight, quarrel, or violent conflict to an end
senses.definitionCN: 使打斗、争吵或暴力冲突结束
senses.example: A single phone call quelled the argument between the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 一通电话就让邻居间的争吵平息了。
senses.why: Physical contests are like small rebellions, so ending a fight keeps the picture of pressing down on motion.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的较量就像小型的反抗，所以结束打斗仍然沿用「把动势按下去」的画面。

senses.title: A clear and forceful calm
senses.definition: to make something lively, noisy, or restless become calm and still
senses.definitionCN: 使喧闹、活跃或躁动的事物变得平静静止
senses.example: The breeze quelled the tiny waves on the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 微风平息了湖面上的细浪。
senses.why: The result of pressing down is stillness, so the verb occasionally describes any restless motion that settles into quiet.
senses.whyCN: 按压的结果是静止，所以这个动词偶尔也用来描述任何躁动的运动归于平静。

intro.en: Quell comes from Old English cwellan, to kill, a word of Germanic origin related to German quälen, to torment; the modern sense is a softening of that killing.
intro.cn: quell 来自古英语 cwellan（杀死），属日耳曼语源，与德语 quälen（折磨）同源；现代义是「杀死」的软化。

items.en: Reconstructed forms such as kwaljan mean to torment or to cause to die.
items.cn: 重构形式如 kwaljan 表示「折磨」或「使死亡」。

items.en: Cwellan means to kill or to murder outright.
items.cn: cwellan 意为「杀死、杀害」。

items.en: The spelling shifts towards quellen and the meaning widens to putting down.
items.cn: 拼写逐渐变为 quellen，含义扩展为「压服」。

items.en: Quell is used for putting down a rebellion or riot.
items.cn: quell 用来表示镇压叛乱或暴乱。

items.en: The sense extends to calming emotions such as fear and anger.
items.cn: 词义扩展到平息恐惧、愤怒等情绪。

items.en: Literary and journalistic use keeps quell chiefly for riots, fears and doubts.
items.cn: 现代文学与新闻用法中，quell 主要用于骚乱、恐惧与疑虑。

note.en: Quell is close to suppress, subdue and crush, but slightly more literary than the everyday stop, and its look-alikes lie in the same Old English killing root.
note.cn: quell 与 suppress、subdue、crush 接近，比日常的 stop 稍显文雅，形近同源词都出自古英语「杀死」这一词根。

entries.definition: to put out a fire or satisfy thirst
entries.definitionCN: 扑灭火焰或解渴；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to reject or cancel a decision officially
entries.definitionCN: 正式撤销或否决决定；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to cause someone or something to die
entries.definitionCN: 杀死，与 quell 同出古英语 cwellan

entries.definition: to stop something by force and keep it from appearing
entries.definitionCN: 武力制止并使其不再出现

entries.definition: to bring a person or feeling under control
to stop something firmly and quickly

normalIntro.en: Quell carries the old idea of killing, softened into putting an uprising down, outward or inward.
normalIntro.cn: quell 带着「杀死」的旧义，软化成把反叛压下去，无论是外在的还是内心的。

normal.en: The verb has doubled in past forms: quelled, quelling and quells.
normal.cn: 这个词过去式与现在分词都双写：quelled、quelling，三单是 quells。

normal.en: Quell fears is a common pairing in news writing.
normal.cn: quell fears（消除恐惧）是新闻写作中的常见搭配。

normal.en: Quell the unrest and quell the riot both describe a crowd being controlled.
normal.cn: quell the unrest 与 quell the riot 都形容人群被控制住。

normal.en: Compare quench, which puts out a fire, while quell puts down trouble.
normal.cn: 对比 quench：quench 扑灭火，quell 压住麻烦。

normal.en: Related German quälen means to torment, which hints at the older sense of bringing suffering to an end.
normal.cn: 同源的德语 quälen 意为折磨，暗示了「让痛苦结束」这个更早的含义。

abstract.en: Picture a firm hand pressed flat on boiling water until the bubbles fade.
abstract.cn: 想象一只坚定的手掌平按在沸水上，直到气泡消失。

abstract.en: Think of a lid pushed down on a pot of fear before it spills over.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅恐惧即将溢出时被盖子硬压回去。

abstract.en: Imagine a crowd shouting and suddenly growing silent.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人大声喊叫，忽然全部安静下来。

examples.en: Extra police were needed to quell the violence.
examples.cn: 需要增派警察来平息暴力事件。

examples.en: Her calm voice quelled the panic in the room.
examples.cn: 她平静的声音平息了房间里的恐慌。

examples.en: The government tried to quell all criticism of the plan.
examples.cn: 政府试图压制对该计划的一切批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「快哦」——闹事的人看到军警就喊「快哦」，于是局面被压下去了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 西日耳曼语 *kwaljan（折磨、使死）→ 古英语 cwellan（杀死）→ 中古英语 quellen（压服）→ 现代英语 quell（镇压；平息），核心义「把翻腾的东西按下去」。

sensesIntro.en: Quell begins with killing, softens into putting down violence, then spreads inward to emotions and outward to any conflict or restless motion.
sensesIntro.cn: quell 从「杀死」出发，软化为压住暴力，进而向内指压制情绪，向外指平息冲突甚至任何躁动的运动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat hand pressing down on boiling water until it is still.
core.cn: 核心意象：手掌按在沸水上，直到水面平静。

branches.en: Putting down violence is the direct heir of the killing sense.
branches.cn: 镇压暴力是「杀死」义的直接继承。

branches.en: Emotions are treated as inner riots to be calmed.
branches.cn: 情绪被当作内心的骚乱来平息。

branches.en: Political criticism is another uprising that is pressed down.
branches.cn: 政治批评是另一场被压下去的反叛。

branches.en: Any fight or restless motion can settle, keeping the picture of a hand on water.
branches.cn: 任何打斗或躁动都可归于平静，仍是手掌压水的画面。

branches.en: All three share the act of stopping something with force.
branches.cn: 前三个义项共享「用力制止」这一行为。

intro.en: Quell is a short Germanic verb with no productive prefixes, but it has a small English family through -er, -ing and un-.
intro.cn: quell 是简短的日耳曼语动词，没有能产的词缀，但通过 -er、-ing 与 un- 形成了小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no direct cognate; the nearest learned relatives come from nec- or inter- words rather than from this root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有直接同源词，最近的学术相关词来自 nec- 或 inter- 一系，而非这个词根。

items.example: Quell is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: quell 是这个词族的基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -er forms queller.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 queller。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms the noun quelling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成名词 quelling。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unquelled.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unquelled。

items.example: Queller is rare but literary.
items.exampleCN: queller 少见但属于文学用法。

items.example: Unquelled describes resistance that goes on.
items.exampleCN: unquelled 描述仍在继续的抵抗。

items.meaning: to put out fire or thirst
items.example: Quench is often confused with quell.
items.exampleCN: quench 常与 quell 混淆。

items.example: Quash is mainly legal.
items.exampleCN: quash 主要用于法律语境。

items.example: Suppress gives the formal near synonym.
items.exampleCN: suppress 提供正式近义词。

items.example: Subdue focuses on people rather than scenes.
items.exampleCN: subdue 更侧重对人而非场面。

definition_zh: 疑问；询问；质疑；查询
definition_en: a question that asks for information or shows doubt, or the act of asking such a question
core_image: 一个人举起手，把问号递到对方眼前，等一个回答
scene: 会议开到一半，有人对报告里的数字起了疑心，举手示意。During the review, an analyst sent a short query to the finance team about a missing figure.
sceneCN: 这里 query 是「疑问、询问」（第 1 个义项：为求澄清而提出的问题）；句意：审阅时，一位分析师就一个缺失的数字向财务团队发了一条简短的询问。

derivatives.zh: 由 query 加 -ed 构成，指被质疑或受查询的数据
复数形式，也指数据库中被提交的一批查询
动名词，指提出询问或执行查询的过程

senses.title: A question that asks for information
senses.definition: a question you ask when you want information or an explanation
senses.definitionCN: 为获取信息或解释而提出的问题
senses.example: If you have any queries about the course, please email the office.
senses.exampleCN: 如果你对课程有任何疑问，请给办公室发邮件。
senses.why: The root quaerere means to seek, and a query is a search for an answer, so any request for information fits.
senses.whyCN: 词根 quaerere 意为「寻找」，query 就是寻找答案，因此任何寻求信息的问题都适用。

senses.title: A question that signals doubt
senses.definition: a question that shows you doubt the truth or fairness of something
senses.definitionCN: 显示你不相信某事的真实性或合理性的提问
senses.example: The judge noted a query about the witness statement.
senses.exampleCN: 法官注意到对证人陈述的一处质疑。
senses.why: Seeking can also mean probing, so the same word turns a simple search into a challenge to what was said.
senses.whyCN: 「寻找」也可以变成「追问」，于是同一个词把单纯的搜索变成对说法的挑战。

senses.title: To question whether something is true
senses.definition: to express doubt about the truth, value, or fairness of something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的真实性、价值或公平性表示怀疑
senses.example: Several members queried the accuracy of the figures.
senses.exampleCN: 几位成员对这些数字的准确性提出质疑。
senses.why: As a verb, the noun meaning of doubt becomes an action, which is why it usually takes a fact or figure as its object.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，名词中「怀疑」的含义转成动作，所以它的宾语通常是事实或数据。

senses.title: A request sent to a database or system
senses.definition: an instruction that asks a database or computer system for specific information
senses.definitionCN: 向数据库或计算机系统请求特定信息的指令
senses.example: The query returned a list of orders from the last month.
senses.exampleCN: 这次查询返回了过去一个月的订单列表。
senses.why: Computing reuses the older picture of asking for something, and a system answers with data the way a person answers
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域沿用了「请求某物」的旧画面，系统像人一样用数据来回答。

senses.title: A formal question in a legal or official setting
senses.definition: a formal question put to a person or body in an official or legal setting
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或法律场合向某人或机构提出的正式问题
senses.example: The committee sent a written query to the ministry about the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会就预算向部里发出了书面质询。
senses.why: In law and public affairs the verb to question was once common, and this formal sense survives in legal records and queries to public bodies.
senses.whyCN: 在法律与公共事务中，动词「加以质疑」曾经很常用，这一正式义保留在法律文书与对公共机构的质询里。

intro.en: Query is a shortening of Latin quaere, to ask, with the quer- root of quaerere, to seek; it enters English through medieval Latin usage and means both a question and the act of seeking.
intro.cn: query 是拉丁语 quaere（问）的缩略，词根 quer- 出自 quaerere（寻找）；它经由中世纪拉丁语用法进入英语，兼指「问题」与「寻求」的动作。

items.en: The root seen in quaerere is linked to seeking, a bold reconstruction rather than an attested form.
items.cn: quaerere 所见的词根与「寻找」有关，这是重构形式，并非实际文献形式。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek or to ask, and quaere is the imperative, to ask or to find out.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻找或询问，quaere 是命令式，意为「去问」「去查明」。

items.en: Quere is written in margins to mark a point to be examined.
items.cn: quere 被写在页边，用来标记需要查核的地方。

items.en: Query enters English as a noun meaning a question or a mark of doubt.
items.cn: query 以名词形式进入英语，指问题或表疑问的记号。

items.en: The verb use develops, meaning to ask about or to doubt.
items.cn: 动词用法发展起来，表示询问或怀疑。

items.en: The word spreads into databases and search tools as a request for data.
items.cn: 这个词延伸到数据库与搜索工具，成为对数据的请求。

note.en: Query belongs to the seeking family of quaerere, with Question and Inquire as close cousins, and it sits beside asks and doubts in meaning.
note.cn: query 属于 quaerere 的「寻求」词族，与 Question、Inquire 是近亲，在意义上也挨着「询问」与「怀疑」这一类词。

entries.definitionCN: 寻求回答的疑问句，与 query 同源

entries.definition: to ask for information formally
entries.definitionCN: 正式询问，与 query 共享 quer- 词根

entries.definition: to take control of a place or people
entries.definitionCN: 征服，同出拉丁语 quaerere 的复合词

to feel unsure about something
the act of asking for information

normalIntro.en: Query is a searching word: its root quaerere means to seek, and every query is a search for an answer or for data.
normalIntro.cn: query 是一个「寻找」的词：词根 quaerere 意为寻找，每一次 query 都是在寻找答案或数据。

normal.en: Raise a query means to put a question forward politely.
normal.cn: raise a query 表示客气地提出问题。

normal.en: Have a query about something is a very common service phrase.
normal.cn: have a query about 是服务场景中极常见的说法。

normal.en: The plural and the verb third person are both spelled queries.
normal.cn: 复数与动词三单的拼写都是 queries。

normal.en: Compare question, inquire and enquiry, which share the quer- root or the same meaning field.
normal.cn: 对比 question、inquire、enquiry，它们共享 quer- 词根或处于同一意义场。

normal.en: The Latin root quaer- shows up in quorum, a word about those who were asked to attend.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 quaer- 也见于 quorum（法定人数），指被要求到场的人。

abstract.cn: 想象在会议上一只手举起，手心画着一个问号。

abstract.en: Imagine a magnifying glass held over a number that does not look right.
abstract.cn: 想象用放大镜对着一个看起来不对劲的数字。

abstract.en: Think of a search box blinking, waiting for you to type and send.
abstract.cn: 想象一个搜索框在闪动，等你输入并发送。

examples.en: Please send any queries to the support desk.
examples.cn: 有任何疑问请发给支持中心。

examples.en: The auditor queried several entries in the account.
examples.cn: 审计师对账目中的几笔记录提出了质疑。

examples.en: A single query can search thousands of records in a second.
examples.cn: 一次查询就能在一秒内检索成千上万条记录。

root: 拉丁语 quaerere（寻找、询问）→ 命令式 quaere（去问）→ 中世纪拉丁语页边标记 quere → 英语 query（疑问；询问；查询），核心义「寻求答案」。

sensesIntro.en: Query begins as a search for an answer, turns into a challenge when doubt is added, then works as a verb and finally becomes a system request for data.
sensesIntro.cn: query 起初是寻求答案，加上怀疑后变成质询，再作动词使用，最后成为向系统请求数据的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised with a question mark, waiting for an answer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的手递出一个问号，等着回答。

branches.en: Seeking information is the plain question sense.
branches.cn: 寻求信息是朴素的提问义。

branches.en: A question that carries doubt is the challenging sense.
branches.cn: 带有怀疑的提问是质询义。

branches.en: As a verb, the challenge becomes an action on facts.
branches.cn: 作动词时，质询变成作用于事实的动作。

branches.en: Machines answer requests with data, so queries move into computing.
branches.cn: 机器用数据回应请求，于是查询进入计算机领域。

branches.en: Official questions are the formal version of the everyday ask.
branches.cn: 正式质询是日常提问的正式版本。

intro.en: Query has no English prefix, but its Latin root quer- shows up in question, inquire and conquer, and the word forms a small English family with -ed and -ing.
intro.cn: query 没有英语前缀，但其拉丁词根 quer- 出现在 question、inquire、conquer 里，并通过 -ed 与 -ing 形成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin quaerere means to seek or ask, and quaere is the imperative to ask.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quaerere 意为寻找或询问，quaere 是命令式「去问」。

items.example: Quaere is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: quaere 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: Quaerere gives the seeking root.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 提供「寻求」词根。

items.example: The root quer- appears in question and inquire.
items.exampleCN: 词根 quer- 见于 question 与 inquire。

items.meaning: a question or a data request
items.example: Query keeps both senses.
items.exampleCN: query 兼有两种含义。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms queried.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 queried。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms querying.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 querying。

items.example: Question shares the quer- root.
items.exampleCN: question 共享 quer- 词根。

items.example: Inquire adds the prefix in- to the root.
items.exampleCN: inquire 在词根前加了前缀 in-。

items.example: Conquer shows the root in a very different field.
items.exampleCN: conquer 显示该词根进入了完全不同的领域。

items.example: Acquirer shows the same root in business.
items.exampleCN: acquirer 显示同一词根在商业中的用法。

definition_zh: 狂犬病；恐水症
definition_en: a serious viral disease that attacks the nervous system and is almost always fatal once symptoms appear
core_image: 被病犬咬伤的伤口，病毒顺着神经缓缓爬向大脑
scene: 村里的狗突然发疯、乱咬人，医生立刻给伤者打了疫苗。A dog in the village went mad and bit a child, so the doctor gave the child a rabies vaccine at once.
sceneCN: 这里 rabies 是「狂犬病」（第 1 个义项：由病兽咬伤传染的致命性病毒感染）；句意：村里的狗疯了并咬了一个孩子，所以医生立刻给孩子注射了狂犬病疫苗。

pos.zh: 狂犬病；恐水症（不可数名词，为医学与日常通用说法）

forms.label: 形容词（由 rabies 加 -ic 构成）

derivatives.zh: 患狂犬病的；疯狂的（源自同一拉丁词根 rabere，后引申为态度极端狂热）
狂怒地；狂热地（rabid 加副词后缀 -ly）
狂怒；狂热（rabid 加名词后缀 -ity 构成的名词）

senses.title: The disease itself
senses.definition: a severe viral infection of the nervous system that spreads through the saliva of infected animals
senses.definitionCN: 由患病动物唾液传播、侵袭神经系统的严重病毒感染
senses.example: Rabies is almost always fatal once symptoms begin.
senses.exampleCN: 一旦出现症状，狂犬病几乎总是致命的。
senses.why: Latin rabere means to be mad, so the name first belongs to the madness that the bite produces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rabere 意为发狂，所以这个词最初指被咬后出现的疯狂状态，病名由此而来。

senses.title: The virus that causes it
senses.definition: the virus, carried mainly by dogs and bats, that enters the body through a bite or a scratch
senses.definitionCN: 主要由犬和蝙蝠携带、通过咬伤或抓伤进入体内的病毒
senses.example: The rabies virus travels along nerves towards the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 狂犬病病毒沿着神经向大脑移动。
senses.why: A disease is often named after its cause, so the word also names the virus that brings the madness.
senses.whyCN: 疾病常以病因命名，所以这个词也用来指带来疯狂的病毒本身。

senses.title: The illness as a public threat
senses.titleCN: 狂犬病疫情；狂犬病风险
senses.definition: the disease as a public health danger, especially in places where stray dogs are common
senses.definitionCN: 作为公共卫生威胁的狂犬病，尤指流浪犬普遍的地区
senses.example: Health teams warned of a rabies outbreak in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 卫生团队警告该地区出现狂犬病疫情。
senses.why: The same name covers the whole danger, not just one patient, so it appears in news about outbreaks and control.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不只指单个病人，也涵盖整体的危险，因此常出现在疫情与防控的新闻里。

senses.title: The vaccine or prevention
senses.titleCN: 狂犬病疫苗；狂犬病防治
senses.definition: the shots or measures that protect people before or after a bite from a rabid animal
senses.definitionCN: 被病兽咬伤前后用来保护人的疫苗注射或防治措施
senses.example: The clinic offers rabies shots after animal bites.
senses.exampleCN: 动物咬伤后，诊所提供狂犬病疫苗注射。
senses.why: In the wards the word shifts from the ill to the cure, so rabies shots became the everyday way of naming the treatment.
senses.whyCN: 在诊室里，这个词从疾病转向救治，于是狂犬病疫苗注射成了日常说法。

senses.title: The old name hydrophobia
senses.definition: the old medical name, short for hydrophobia, which describes the patient refusing water
senses.definitionCN: 旧时医学名称，是恐水症一词的简称，描述病人见水便惊
senses.example: Writers of the past called rabies hydrophobia.
senses.exampleCN: 过去的作家把狂犬病称作恐水症。
senses.why: One symptom, a violent fear of water, was once so striking that it replaced the disease name in older medical writing.
senses.whyCN: 病人对水的剧烈恐惧这一症状太触目，以致在旧医学文献里取代了病名。

senses.title: The madness in a rabid animal
senses.definition: the furious, biting behaviour that an infected animal shows
senses.definitionCN: 受感染动物表现出的狂躁乱咬的行为
senses.example: The fox showed rabies and attacked everything in its path.
senses.exampleCN: 那只狐狸表现出狂性，见什么咬什么。
senses.why: Raber means to rave, and the raving animal is the original picture behind the name.
senses.whyCN: raber 意为狂乱发疯，而发狂的动物正是这个词名背后的原始画面。

senses.title: The feverish rule of an itch
senses.definition: in rare and figurative use, a burning frenzy or passion that drives someone on
senses.definitionCN: 罕见而比喻的用法，指驱使人前行的炽烈狂热或冲动
senses.example: Nothing satisfied his rabies for discovery.
senses.exampleCN: 什么都满足不了他那种疯狂的探索欲望。
senses.why: From the literal bite the same root reaches into metaphor, where rabies stands for any unchecked fury.
senses.whyCN: 从字面的咬伤出发，同一词根延伸到比喻层面，rabies 可代表任何不受约束的狂热。

senses.title: The bite that passes the disease
senses.definition: by ordinary use, the dangerous animal bite or scratch that carries the infection
senses.definitionCN: 日常用法中，指带来这种感染的凶险咬伤或抓伤
senses.example: Doctors cleaned the wound and tested for rabies.
senses.exampleCN: 医生清洗伤口，并检测是否染上狂犬病。
senses.why: People name the injury by the disease it can carry, so a wound is checked for rabies rather than for a virus.
senses.whyCN: 人们用可能携带的病名来指称伤口，所以会检查伤口是否有狂犬病，而不是检查某个病毒。

intro.en: Rabies comes from the Latin noun rabies, meaning madness, which grew from the verb rabere, to rave or be mad.
intro.cn: rabies 来自拉丁语名词 rabies（疯狂），由动词 rabere（发狂）演变而来。

items.en: The verb rabere means to rave, to be furious, or to be mad.
items.cn: 动词 rabere 意为狂乱、暴怒或发狂。

items.en: The noun rabies means madness, and colaphus passages show it used of animals as well as people.
items.cn: 名词 rabies 意为疯狂，早期用例既写人发狂，也写动物发狂。

items.en: Writers such as Vergil already use rabies of the fury of dogs or of passion.
items.cn: 维吉尔等作家已用 rabies 描写犬的凶狂或人的激情。

items.en: Medical Latin takes rabies as the name of the disease that makes a dog or a person mad.
items.cn: 医学拉丁语把 rabies 定为使人或犬发狂那种病的名称。

items.en: The word reaches English through medical texts and keeps the disease sense.
items.cn: 这个词经由医学文本进入英语，保留了疾病含义。

items.en: Modern English uses rabies for the disease and its virus, and keeps the older term hydrophobia.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rabies 指病与病毒，并保留旧称「恐水症」。

note.en: Rabies is the Latin madness noun related to rabid and rabidly, and it belongs in the field of infectious animal diseases.
note.cn: rabies 是拉丁语「疯狂」名词，与 rabid、rabidly 同源，属于动物传染病义场。

normalIntro.en: Rabies is the Latin word for madness, and the disease itself is a madness that runs from a bite to the brain.
normalIntro.cn: rabies 本来就是拉丁语的「疯狂」一词，而这场病也正是由咬伤一路跑进大脑的疯狂。

normal.en: Keep the Latin verb rabere in mind: to rave gives the madness at the heart of the name.
normal.cn: 记住拉丁语动词 rabere（发狂）：这份疯狂正是词名的内核。

normal.en: Rabies and rabid share one root, and rabid kept the promise of the word for everyday use.
normal.cn: rabies 与 rabid 同根，而 rabid 把这股狂劲留在了日常说法里。

normal.en: The common phrase rabies vaccine shows how often the word names the cure as well.
normal.cn: 常见搭配 rabies vaccine 表明，这个词也常用来指救治手段。

normal.en: The old name hydrophobia means fear of water, one of the symptoms of the illness.
normal.cn: 旧称 hydrophobia 意为怕水，正是该病的一个症状。

normal.en: Compare distemper: it names another viral disease of animals, and both words sit in the same medical family.
normal.cn: 对比 distemper：它指另一种动物病毒病，这两个词同属一个医学家族。

abstract.en: Picture a stray dog with foam at the mouth on a road in the afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象下午的马路上，一只流浪狗嘴角流着白沫。

abstract.en: Picture the saliva of the bite as a trail of red dots rising along a nerve.
abstract.cn: 把咬伤处的唾液想象成一串红点，沿着神经向上爬升。

abstract.en: Think of a whole town staying indoors while animal teams go from street to street.
abstract.cn: 想象整个小镇闭门不出，而捕犬队一条街一条街地巡查。

examples.en: Rabies is spread mainly through the saliva of infected animals.
examples.cn: 狂犬病主要通过患病动物的唾液传播。

examples.en: Anyone bitten by a stray dog should seek rabies treatment at once.
examples.cn: 被流浪狗咬伤的人应当立刻接受狂犬病治疗。

examples.en: Vaccinating dogs is the cheapest way to control rabies.
examples.cn: 给犬只接种疫苗是控制狂犬病最便宜的办法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞比斯」——被疯狗咬后一路「狂」起来，记住 rabies 就是狂犬病；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rabere（发狂、狂乱）→ 名词 rabies（疯狂；狂犬病）→ 医学拉丁语沿用 → 英语 rabies，核心义「被咬后的疯狂」。

sensesIntro.en: Rabies begins with the disease, then names its virus, its public danger, its vaccine, and finally the old symptom and the metaphor.
sensesIntro.cn: rabies 先指这场疾病，再指它的病毒、它的公共危险、它的疫苗，最后才是旧症状名与比喻用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bite that carries madness along the nerves into the brain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次咬伤，把疯狂沿着神经送进大脑。

branches.en: The disease of the nervous system is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 侵袭神经系统的疾病是字面义项。

branches.en: The virus is the cause named after the disease.
branches.cn: 病毒是以病名指称的病因。

branches.en: A regional outbreak and a rabid animal both describe the danger on the street.
branches.cn: 地区疫情与发狂的动物都描述街头的危险。

branches.en: The vaccine and the wound contrast prevention with risk.
branches.cn: 疫苗与伤口把预防和风险对照起来。

branches.en: The old name hydrophobia and the fiery frenzy both carry the ancient sense of raging fear.
branches.cn: 旧称恐水症与炽烈的狂热都承载了古代「狂暴恐惧」的意味。

intro.en: Rabies is a Latin noun recorded in medical form, and English has built rabid, rabidly, and rabidity around the same stem.
intro.cn: rabies 是拉丁语中以医学形态记录下来的名词，英语围绕同一词干构成 rabid、rabidly 与 rabidity。

latinIntro.en: Latin rabere means to rave, and rabies means madness; the medical use chose the noun for the disease.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rabere 意为狂乱，rabies 意为疯狂；医学用法选中这个名词来命名疾病。

items.example: The root rab- carries the idea of raging fury.
items.exampleCN: 词根 rab- 承载着狂暴的意味。

items.example: Raber is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: rabere 是这一整个词族的动词来源。

items.example: Rabies is the Latin noun for madness.
items.exampleCN: rabies 是拉丁语中「疯狂」的名词。

items.meaning: a fixed form as a noun
items.example: The noun ending -ies marks rabies as a fixed Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 名词词尾 -ies 使 rabies 成为固定的拉丁语形式。

items.example: Rabid describes an animal with the disease.
items.exampleCN: rabid 描述染病的动物。

items.example: The ending -id forms rabid from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -id 由同一词干构成 rabid。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms rabidly from rabid.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 由 rabid 构成 rabidly。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms rabidity from rabid.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 由 rabid 构成 rabidity。

items.example: The prefix hydro- starts the old name hydrophobia.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 hydro- 开始于旧称 hydrophobia。

items.example: The suffix -phobia names the fear in hydrophobia.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -phobia 表达 hydrophobia 中的恐惧。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 医学拉丁语中指狂犬病

definition_zh: 光辉灿烂的；容光焕发的；辐射的
definition_en: sending out light and heat, or showing great happiness that seems to shine from the face
core_image: 一轮太阳从云层后射出光芒，光线向四周散开
scene: 婚礼上的新娘一推门进来，满屋子人都觉得她脸上在发光。When the bride walked in, her radiant face made the whole room seem warmer.
sceneCN: 这里 radiant 是「容光焕发的」（第 1 个义项：神情明亮，像有光从脸上透出）；句意：新娘走进来时，她容光焕发的脸让整个房间都显得温暖了。

pos.zh: 光辉的；容光焕发的；辐射的

derivatives.zh: 光辉；容光（radiant 去掉 -t 加 -ce 构成的名词）
光灿灿地；容光焕发地（radiant 加 -ly）
辐射；放射物（与 radiant 同据 radiate）
辐射；散发（radiant 的动词同源形式）

senses.title: Shining with happiness
senses.titleCN: 容光焕发的；喜气洋溢的
senses.definition: looking so happy and healthy that the feeling seems to glow from the face
senses.definitionCN: 神情快乐健康得仿佛有光从脸上透出来
senses.example: She was radiant when she heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那个消息时，她容光焕发。
senses.why: The Latin root means a beam, so happiness is pictured as light going out from a face.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为光束，所以把快乐想成从脸上射出的光。

senses.title: Sending out light
senses.titleCN: 光辉灿烂的；光芒四射的
senses.definition: sending out strong light, or brightly lit by a source of light
senses.definitionCN: 发出强光，或被光源照得通明
senses.example: A radiant sun broke through the clouds.
senses.exampleCN: 一轮灿烂的太阳从云层中透出来。
senses.why: From the face the light becomes literal, and the word describes what a sun or a lamp actually sends out.
senses.whyCN: 光从脸上转向字面，这个词开始描述太阳或灯实际射出的光。

senses.title: Sending out heat or energy
senses.definition: in physics, transferring heat or energy in waves without a material carrier
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中，以波的形式而不借助物质载体传递热或能量
senses.example: A fire warms a room by radiant heat.
senses.exampleCN: 火以辐射热的方式给房间供暖。
senses.why: Latin radius is both a spoke and a ray, so the spreading of light becomes the spreading of energy in straight lines.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 radius 既指轮辐又指光线，所以光的发散就成了能量沿直线传播。

senses.title: Bright in an abstract way
senses.titleCN: （比喻）光彩照人的；极其美好的
senses.definition: used figuratively of beauty, joy, or a period that seems to shine on everyone
senses.definitionCN: 比喻地用于美、喜悦或一段似乎照亮所有人的时期
senses.example: The letters belong to the radiant years of her youth.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件属于她青春的光辉岁月。
senses.why: A beam that lights up everything around it gives the word a quiet metaphor for a time or a quality that shines.
senses.whyCN: 照亮四周的光束让这个词成为时间或品质闪耀的安静比喻。

senses.title: Rays of a plant
senses.definition: in botany, describing the flower rays that spread out from the centre of an umbrella-like head
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中，描述伞形花序从中心放射状伸出的花辐
senses.example: The daisy carries white radiant petals around its centre.
senses.exampleCN: 雏菊中心周围长着白色的放射状花瓣。
senses.why: Flower parts named by radius echo the picture of spokes opening from a hub, so a flat ray is a radiant ray.
senses.whyCN: 以 radius 命名的花部复现了辐条从轮毂张开的形象，因此平展的花辐就是放射状的花辐。

senses.title: Radiance at a meeting
senses.definition: a formal and literary noun use, as in describing the radiance of a ceremony or a saint
senses.definitionCN: 正式或文学的名词性用法，如形容典礼或圣徒的光辉
senses.example: The ceremony carried a radiant dignity on every face.
senses.exampleCN: 典礼让每一张脸都带上一种光辉的庄严。
senses.why: Formal writing keeps the light image for dignity and honour, where the shine belongs to the occasion.
senses.whyCN: 正式文笔把光的意象留给庄严与荣耀，此时光芒属于整个场合。

intro.en: Radiant comes from Latin radiare, to emit beams, from radius, a spoke of a wheel and also a ray of light.
intro.cn: radiant 来自拉丁语 radiare（射出光束），源于 radius（轮辐，也指光线）。

items.en: Radius first means a spoke of a wheel, and then a ray of light spreading from a centre.
items.cn: radius 先指轮辐，后指从中心射出的光线。

items.en: The verb radiare means to send out rays or to shine.
items.cn: 动词 radiare 意为射出光线、闪耀。

items.en: The participle radiante is the form in use when the word travels out.
items.cn: 传播出去时，使用的正是现在分词形式 radiante。

items.en: French radiant carries the shining sense northwards.
items.cn: 法语的 radiant 把这个闪耀的含义向北传。

items.en: English radiant first describes beams of light and later a shining face.
items.cn: 英语的 radiant 先描写光束，后指发光的脸。

items.en: Modern science adds radiant heat and radiant energy as technical terms.
items.cn: 现代科学新增辐射热与辐射能等技术术语。

note.en: Radiant is the adjective of the radius family, close to radiance and the verb radiate, and it sits with words for light and joy.
note.cn: radiant 是 radius 词族的形容词，与 radiance、动词 radiate 相邻，并与表示光与喜悦的词同场。

entries.definition: great brightness or a glow of happiness
to send out light, heat, or a feeling
a straight line from the centre of a circle to its edge
giving out light, especially a soft and steady light
smiling very happily and openly
shining warmly, or full of praise

normalIntro.en: Radiant is built on Latin radius, a spoke and a ray: something goes out from a centre in straight lines.
normalIntro.cn: radiant 建立在拉丁语 radius（轮辐、光线）之上：有东西从中心沿直线射出。

normal.en: The same stem gives radius, radiate, radiation, and radiance, so the family all deals with rays.
normal.cn: 同一词干生出 radius、radiate、radiation 与 radiance，这一族都与光线有关。

normal.en: Pair the adjective with common phrases: a radiant smile, radiant health, radiant heat.
normal.cn: 把这个形容词与常见搭配成对记：灿烂的笑容、容光焕发、辐射热。

normal.en: Radiant heat is a technical phrase, and it shows the physics sense hidden in an everyday word.
normal.cn: 辐射热是技术性搭配，它揭示了日常词汇里藏着的物理学义项。

normal.en: Compare shine and glow: both are verbs, while radiant describes a state.
normal.cn: 对比 shine 与 glow：两者都是动词，而 radiant 描述一种状态。

normal.en: A wheel spoke and a sunbeam share the name radius, which is why brightness and spreading are one idea.
normal.cn: 轮辐与太阳光同用一个名字 radius，所以「明亮」与「发散」是同一个概念。

abstract.en: Picture a bride at the door, and the room turning brighter as she smiles.
abstract.cn: 想象新娘站在门口，她一笑，整个房间都变亮了。

abstract.en: Picture spokes of light leaving a lamp in every direction at once.
abstract.cn: 想象灯光像轮辐一样向四面八方射出。

abstract.en: Think of a heater warming your hands with light you cannot see.
abstract.cn: 想象暖炉用你看不见的光暖热你的手。

examples.en: The morning was radiant after the rain.
examples.cn: 雨后的清晨一片灿烂。

examples.en: He gave her a radiant smile across the table.
examples.cn: 他隔着桌子给了她一个灿烂的笑容。

examples.en: Radiant energy from the sun drives the weather.
examples.cn: 来自太阳的辐射能驱动着天气变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞迪恩特」——瑞气洋洋、光「迪」出来、恩「特」耀眼的一个人，记成容光焕发的；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 radius（轮辐；光线）→ radiare（放射、闪耀）→ 现在分词 radiante → 法语 radiant → 英语 radiant，核心义「光从中心射向四方」。

sensesIntro.en: Radiant starts from a face that seems to shine, moves to real light and then to radiated energy, and ends in metaphor and formal usage.
sensesIntro.cn: radiant 从一张仿佛发光的面孔开始，转到真实的光，再转到被辐射的能量，最后落到比喻与正式用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rays leaving a centre, like spokes from a hub or light from the sun.
core.cn: 核心意象：光从中心射出，像辐条出于轮毂、像阳光出于太阳。

branches.en: The glowing face is the first and warmest sense.
branches.cn: 发光的脸是最先、最温暖的义项。

branches.en: Real light from a sun or lamp is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 太阳或灯发出的真实光线是字面义项。

branches.en: Radiant heat and flower rays keep the straight-line picture of rays.
branches.cn: 辐射热与花辐都保留了射线沿直线展开的画面。

branches.en: Beautiful years and formal honour use the light as a quiet metaphor.
branches.cn: 美好岁月与正式的荣耀把光用作安静的比喻。

branches.en: A shining face and a shining sun share one description because both send out light.
branches.cn: 发亮的脸与发亮的太阳共享一个描述，因为两者都在发光。

intro.en: Radiant is built on the Latin stem radi-, with -ant making it an adjective; English also has radiate, radiation, and radiance.
intro.cn: radiant 建立在拉丁词干 radi- 上，由 -ant 构成形容词；英语还有 radiate、radiation 与 radiance。

latinIntro.en: Latin radius means a spoke or a ray, and radiare means to send out rays, which yields the participle radiante.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 radius 意为轮辐或光线，radiare 意为射出光线，由此得到分词 radiante。

items.example: The root radi- names a line running out from a centre.
items.exampleCN: 词根 radi- 指从中心向外延伸的线。

items.meaning: a spoke of a wheel, a ray
items.example: Radius is the noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: radius 是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: Radiare means to shine like a sun.
items.exampleCN: radiare 意为像太阳一样闪耀。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ant forms radiant from the participle stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 由分词词干构成 radiant。

items.meaning: to send out light or heat
items.example: Radiate keeps the Latin verb sense.
items.exampleCN: radiate 保留拉丁语动词含义。

items.meaningCN: 过程或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms radiation from radiate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 由 radiate 构成 radiation。

items.example: The suffix -ance forms radiance beside radiant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 与 radiant 并立构成 radiance。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms radiantly from radiant.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 由 radiant 构成 radiantly。

items.example: Radiation names energy travelling in waves.
items.exampleCN: radiation 指以波的形式传播的能量。

items.example: Radiance names the quality of being radiant.
items.exampleCN: radiance 表示「有光辉」这一性质。

definition_zh: 根本地；彻底地；激进地
definition_en: in a way that goes to the root of something, so that the whole thing changes completely
core_image: 一棵树被连根拔起，根须暴露在地面上
scene: 老城区改造时，推土机一来，整条街的样子都不同了。When the old district was rebuilt, the shops and streets changed radically within a year.
sceneCN: 这里 radically 是「彻底地」（第 1 个义项：改变到根基之处）；句意：老城区重建后，商店和街道在一年内彻底变了样。

derivatives.zh: 根本的；激进的（radically 去掉 -ly 的基础形容词）
激进主义（radical 加 -ism）
使激进（radical 加 -ize 的动词化形式）
激进化（radicalize 加 -ation）

senses.title: To the root
senses.definition: in a way that affects the deepest and most basic part of something
senses.definitionCN: 以影响事物最深、最基本部分的方式
senses.example: The move radically changed her daily routine.
senses.exampleCN: 这次搬家彻底改变了她的日常作息。
senses.why: Latin radix is a root, so what is done radically touches the root rather than the surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 radix 意为根，因此以 radically 行事的做法触到的是根而非表面。

senses.title: A completely different state
senses.definition: used of two things that differ so much that they belong to different orders
senses.definitionCN: 用于差异极大、分属不同层次的两件事
senses.example: The two proposals are radically different.
senses.exampleCN: 这两份提案截然不同。
senses.why: If a change reaches the root, the before and after no longer share a base, so they look entirely separate.
senses.whyCN: 如果变化直达根基，前后就不再共用同一个基础，因此看起来分属两样。

senses.title: In politics, going to extremes
senses.definition: in politics, in a way that wants deep and fast change of the existing system
senses.definitionCN: 政治上一心要深而快地改变现有制度的立场
senses.example: Some groups campaigned radically against the new law.
senses.exampleCN: 一些团体以激进的方式反对这项新法律。
senses.why: Political radical first wanted change at the root of the system, and over time it also took on the flavour of going to extremes.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的 radical 起初要从制度根上改变，久而久之也带上了走极端的意味。

senses.title: From the bottom up in maths
senses.definition: in mathematics, of or by a root sign or a root quantity
senses.definitionCN: 数学中涉及根号或根式地
senses.example: The equation can be solved radically.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程可以用根式方法求解。
senses.why: The same Latin radix names a root of a number, which is why a radical sign is a root sign.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁词 radix 也指数的一个根，所以 radical 号就是根号。

senses.title: Of the root in plants and words
senses.titleCN: （植物）根部的；（语言学）词根方面的
senses.definition: in botany and grammar, relating to the root of a plant or the root of a word
senses.definitionCN: 植物学与语法中，与植物的根或词的词根相关
senses.example: Speech therapists treat problems radically.
senses.exampleCN: 言语治疗师从词根层面处理问题。
senses.why: The literal root in soil is the model for the root of a word, so language is described in the same terms.
senses.whyCN: 土壤里实物的根是词根的模型，因此语言也用同一套说法来描述。

intro.en: Radically comes from radical, from Latin radicalis, from radix, a root; the word reaches its roots of things.
intro.cn: radically 来自 radical，而 radical 出自拉丁语 radicalis，源于 radix（根），本义与事物的根有关。

items.en: Radix means a root, either of a plant or of a number.
items.cn: radix 意为根，既可指植物的根，也可指数的一个根。

items.en: Radicalis means of the root, and it is used in grammar and in counting.
items.cn: radicalis 意为属于根的，用于语法与计数。

items.en: Medieval grammar writers use radicalis for the stem or root of a word.
items.cn: 中世纪语法作家用 radicalis 指一个词的词干或词根。

items.en: Radical enters English with the root sense, first in learned writing.
items.cn: radical 以「根」的含义进入英语，最初见于学术写作。

items.en: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries radical also names deep political change.
items.cn: 到了十八、十九世纪，radical 也用来指深刻的政治变革。

items.en: The adverb radically grows from the adjective to mean in a root-deep way.
items.cn: 副词 radically 由形容词发展而来，表示「深及根本地」。

note.en: Radically is the adverb of radical, close to radic and its relatives, and it belongs with adverbs of deep change such as completely and thoroughly.
note.cn: radically 是 radical 的副词形式，与 radic 词根及其亲属词相近，并与 completely、thoroughly 这类表示深刻改变的副词同场。

entries.definition: relating to the root, or wanting deep change
the belief in deep and fast political change
a small red or white root vegetable
in every way, with nothing missing
in a careful and detailed way
at the most basic level

normalIntro.en: Radically comes from Latin radix, a root: to do something radically is to work at the root of the matter, not on its skin.
normalIntro.cn: radically 来自拉丁语 radix（根）：彻底地做一件事，就是在事情的根上动手，而不是在表皮上。

normal.en: The same root gives radical, radicalism, and radish, the last one being the root vegetable.
normal.cn: 同一词根生出 radical、radicalism 与 radish，最后一个正是萝卜这种根菜。

normal.en: Pair it with change and difference: radically different is the most frequent pattern.
normal.cn: 它与 change、difference 常搭配：radically different 是最常见的组合。

normal.en: In politics, radical keeps the older sense of wanting change at the root of the system.
normal.cn: 在政治语境里，radical 保留着「要在制度根上求变」的旧义。

normal.en: Compare fundamentally, which names the base, while radically names the root and its depth.
normal.cn: 对比 fundamentally：它讲的是基础，radically 讲的是根与深度。

normal.en: The word comes from the Latin for root, so an agent that works radically works from the bottom.
normal.cn: 这个词源于拉丁语的根，因此以 radically 起作用的因素是从底下动起来的。

abstract.en: Picture a tree pulled up by its roots and lying on the lawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树被连根拔起，横躺在草坪上。

abstract.en: Imagine a house whose walls have been cut away from the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子的墙体整个被人从地面上拆开。

abstract.en: Think of a street where every shop sign has been painted a new colour overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街的店铺招牌一夜之间全换了颜色。

examples.en: The new teaching method was radically different from the old one.
examples.cn: 新的教学方法与旧的截然不同。

examples.en: Prices have fallen radically since the reform began.
examples.cn: 自改革开始以来，物价已大幅下降。

examples.en: Critics argued that the plan would radically alter the city.
examples.cn: 批评者认为该计划会彻底改变这座城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞迪克利」——想象把一棵树「连」根拔「起」，「利」落地彻底翻个底朝天，记成彻底地；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 radix（根）→ radicalis（属于根的）→ 英语 radical（根本的）→ radically（从根本上；彻底地），核心义「在根处」。

sensesIntro.en: Radically starts at the root of a thing, then describes a completely different state, then political extremes, and finally the literal root senses in maths, plants, and words.
sensesIntro.cn: radically 从事物的根开始，再表示截然不同的状态，然后是政治上的极端，最后回到数学、植物与词汇中字面的「根」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plant pulled up by its roots, so nothing of the old position is left.
core.cn: 核心意象：一株植物被连根拔起，原有的位置一点也不剩。

branches.en: Touching the deepest part is the central adverb sense.
branches.cn: 触及最深的部分是核心副词义项。

branches.en: A change at the root leaves two things completely unlike.
branches.cn: 根上的改变使两样东西彻底不同。

branches.en: Political radicalism asks for fast, root-level change.
branches.cn: 政治上的激进主义要求的正是快速、触及根本的改变。

branches.en: The root of a number, a plant, and a word all keep the literal Latin sense.
branches.cn: 数的根、植物的根、词的根都保留了拉丁语的字面含义。

branches.en: Root-deep and entirely different usually describe the same change from two angles.
branches.cn: 「深及根本」与「截然不同」常是从两个角度描述同一种变化。

intro.en: Radically is radical plus -ly; the Latin stem radic- comes from the noun radix, a root.
intro.cn: radically 是 radical 加 -ly；拉丁词干 radic- 出自名词 radix（根）。

latinIntro.en: Latin radix means a root, and radicalis means of the root; the family spread from there into grammar and politics.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 radix 意为根，radicalis 意为属于根的；这一族由此外扩到语法与政治。

items.example: The root radic- carries the image of a root.
items.exampleCN: 词根 radic- 承载着「根」的意象。

items.example: Radix is the noun behind radical.
items.exampleCN: radix 是 radical 背后的名词。

items.example: Radicalis gives English radical.
items.exampleCN: radicalis 给出英语的 radical。

items.example: The suffix -al forms radical from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 由拉丁词干构成 radical。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms radically from radical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 由 radical 构成 radically。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms radicalism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 radicalism。

items.example: The suffix -ize forms radicalize.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ize 构成 radicalize。

items.meaningCN: 过程或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ation forms radicalization.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 radicalization。

items.example: Radish comes through Old English from the same root.
items.exampleCN: radish 经由古英语出自同一词根。

items.meaning: to pull out by the roots
items.example: Eradicate adds the prefix e- to the root of radix.
items.exampleCN: eradicate 在 radix 的根前加上前缀 e-。

items.meaning: the first root of a seedling
items.example: Radicle names the small first root.
items.exampleCN: radicle 指最初的小根。

definition_zh: 萝卜；萝卜根；小萝卜头
definition_en: a small vegetable with a round or long root that is usually eaten raw in salads
core_image: 白色或红色的圆萝卜缨叶下拔出泥土根，脆生生咬一口
scene: 菜园里，孩子把一颗红皮白心的圆萝卜从松软的土里拔出来，抖掉泥，当场咬了一口。In the sunny garden, the children pulled a crisp radish from the soft soil and ate it on the spot.
sceneCN: 这里 radish 是「萝卜」（第 1 个义项：一种脆嫩可生吃的根菜植物）；句意：在阳光下的菜园里，孩子们从松软的土里拔出一颗脆萝卜，当场就吃了。

derivatives.zh: 萝卜的；带萝卜味的：由 radish 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，形容像萝卜或萝卜味
辣根：由 horse（意为粗大、猛烈）加 radish 复合而成，指味道猛烈的近亲植物
萝卜（复数）：radish 的规则复数形式，仍表示这种根菜或它的可食部分

senses.title: The root vegetable
senses.definition: a small root vegetable, usually round or long, with a white, red, or pink skin and a crisp, peppery flesh
senses.definitionCN: 一种小型根茎蔬菜，呈圆形或长形，表皮为白色、红色或粉红色，肉质脆而带辛味
senses.example: She sliced a radish into the salad.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一颗萝卜切片放进沙拉。
senses.why: The Latin word radix means root, and the vegetable is named for the swollen root we eat.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 radix 意为「根」，这种蔬菜正是以我们食用的膨大根部而得名。

senses.title: The edible root alone
senses.definition: the firm white or red part of the plant, eaten raw or cooked
senses.definitionCN: 这种植物坚实可食的白色或红色部分，可生吃也可烹煮
senses.example: The grilled fish comes with shredded radish.
senses.exampleCN: 烤鱼配了萝卜丝。
senses.why: The same word can point not at the whole plant but at the root on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词可以不指整株植物，而专指盘子里的那块根。

senses.title: A small token as a unit
senses.definition: a single vegetable as a countable item, as when buying or counting
senses.definitionCN: 作为可数个体的一颗体积单位，用于购买或计数
senses.example: We planted twelve radishes along the fence.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着篱笆种了十二棵萝卜。
senses.why: Because Count usage turns the mass of plants into separate edible units, the plural radishes names pieces you can hold.
senses.whyCN: 因为可数用法把整片植株拆成一颗颗能拿在手里的单位，所以复数 radishes 指可以点的具体个体。

senses.title: The plant itself
senses.definition: the plant that produces these roots, grown in gardens and farms
senses.definitionCN: 产生这种根部的植株，通常种在菜园或农场中
senses.example: Radish plants grow quickly in cool weather.
senses.exampleCN: 萝卜植株在凉爽的天气里长得很快。
senses.why: From the edible root the word naturally extends to the whole leafy plant in the ground.
senses.whyCN: 从可食用的根义自然延伸到地里整株带叶的植物。

senses.title: A general term for root crops
senses.definition: a loose name for several root crops of the same family, such as the winter radish and the black radish
senses.definitionCN: 对同科若干根菜（如大根萝卜、黑萝卜）的泛称
senses.example: Farmers here grow two kinds of radish for the winter market.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农民为冬季市场种两种萝卜。
senses.why: Because many similar root crops share the name, radish can act as a family label rather than one species.
senses.whyCN: 因为许多相似的根菜共用这个词，radish 可以充当类名而不指单一物种。

senses.title: The peppery flavour note
senses.definition: the sharp, slightly hot taste typical of fresh radish
senses.definitionCN: 新鲜萝卜特有的尖锐微辣味道
senses.example: A little horseradish gives the sauce a radish kick.
senses.exampleCN: 一点辣根给酱汁带来萝卜般的辛辣刺激。
senses.why: The taste of the root is so distinctive that its name becomes a way to describe flavour.
senses.whyCN: 萝卜的味道太有辨识度，以至于它的名字成了一种描述风味的说法。

senses.title: A cheap or humble thing
senses.definition: something cheap or of little value, especially in informal talk
senses.definitionCN: 便宜或毫不起眼的事物，多见于口语
senses.example: He traded his old bike for a radish of a watch.
senses.exampleCN: 他用旧自行车换了一块不值钱的表。
senses.why: Peasant food gave the root a humble image, so the word can stand for anything cheap.
senses.whyCN: 萝卜是平民蔬菜，因此这个词也能代指便宜、不起眼的东西。

senses.title: A term of mock praise
senses.definition: a playful or teasing name for a person, especially a clumsy or stubborn one
senses.definitionCN: 对某人（尤指笨拙或固执的人）的戏称
senses.example: The coach called the clumsy rookie a little radish.
senses.exampleCN: 教练把笨手笨脚的新人称作小萝卜头。
senses.why: Round and squat as the vegetable is, the name lends itself to affectionate mockery of small people or odd shapes.
senses.whyCN: 萝卜又圆又矮的样子，让这个词很适合亲切地揶揄小个子或古怪的外形。

senses.title: A symbol of simple country life
senses.definition: in literature, an emblem of plain rural food and honest poverty
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中象征朴素的乡村食物与清贫质朴
senses.example: In the poem, boiled radish stands for a farmer peace.
senses.exampleCN: 在诗中，水煮萝卜象征农家的安宁。
senses.why: For thousands of years this root fed ordinary families, so writers use it as shorthand for a plain, honest life.
senses.whyCN: 几千年来这种根菜养活了普通人家，所以作家用它来简写朴素诚实的生活。

intro.en: Radish comes from Latin radix, root, through Old English rædic and Old French radis.
intro.cn: radish 追溯至拉丁语 radix（根），经古英语 rædic 与古法语 radis 传入现代英语。

items.en: Radix means a root, the part of a plant that grows under the ground.
items.cn: 拉丁语 radix 意为根，即植物长在地下的部分。

items.en: Rædic appears in Old English for the root vegetable.
items.cn: 古英语公元十世纪已有 rædic，指这种根菜。

items.en: Old French radis names the same vegetable.
items.cn: 古法语 radis 指同一种蔬菜。

items.en: Radish enters English as a garden and market word.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 radish 作为菜园与市场用词进入英语。

items.en: Compounds such as horseradish build on the same root.
items.cn: 现代英语由同一词根构成 horseradish（辣根）等复合词。

note.en: Radish is the root-named vegetable, close in spelling to radius and radix, and near in meaning to other roots and vegetables.
note.cn: radish 是以「根」命名的蔬菜，拼写上接近 radius、radix，意义上靠近其他根菜与蔬菜词。

entries.definition: the distance from the centre of a circle to its edge
entries.definitionCN: 半径：与 radish 同源自「根」，但意义完全不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a root, especially in mathematics or computing
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「根」；基数，是 radish 的直接源头

entries.definition: the first small root of a plant embryo
entries.definitionCN: 胚根：与 radish 同出 radix，指种子长出的第一条细根（读音与 radical 不同）

entries.definition: relating to the root or to deep change
entries.definitionCN: 根本的；激进的：同出 radix，义为「从根上」

entries.definition: a strong hot root used as a condiment
entries.definitionCN: 辣根：horse 加 radish 构成的复合词

entries.definition: a long orange root vegetable
entries.definitionCN: 胡萝卜：同为根菜，颜色与形状不同

entries.definition: a round white root vegetable
entries.definitionCN: 芜菁：外形相近的白色根菜，属于不同科

entries.definition: a dark red root vegetable
entries.definitionCN: 甜菜根：另一种可生食的根菜

normalIntro.en: Radish keeps the Latin root in plain sight: radix means root, and the vegetable is the swollen root we dig up.
normalIntro.cn: radish 把拉丁词根摆在明面上：radix 意为根，这种蔬菜就是我们挖出来的膨大根部。

normal.en: Radish and radix share one Latin root, and both point down into the soil.
normal.cn: radish 与 radix 同出一个拉丁根词，都指向泥土之下的部分。

normal.en: Radix also gives radius and radical, so the root idea runs through three everyday words.
normal.cn: radix 也衍生出 radius 与 radical，于是「根」的意象贯穿三个日常词。

normal.en: The plural keeps the -es, and it is pronounced iz, not es with a z sound spelled plainly.
normal.cn: 复数写成 radishes，结尾读作 iz，而不是一个单独的 z 音。

normal.en: Radish is in the usual collocations white radish and red radish, eaten raw in salads.
normal.cn: radish 常见于 white radish 与 red radish 等搭配，多生吃做沙拉。

normal.en: Horseradish joins horse, meaning strong and coarse, to radish, the mild vegetable.
normal.cn: horseradish 把表示「粗猛」的 horse 与温和的 radish 拼在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling a red-white root out of dark soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从黑土里拔出一颗红白相间的根。

abstract.en: Hear the crunch when the root is cut, and link the sound to the short vowel æ.
abstract.cn: 想象切开根部时的脆响，把这种声音和短元音 æ 连起来。

abstract.en: See a thin root thread running down, just like the root syllable in radius.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细细的根须垂下去，正像 radius 里那个根词音节。

examples.en: The salad was topped with sliced red radishes.
examples.cn: 沙拉上铺满了切片红萝卜。

examples.en: Farmers here grow radish and cabbage in the cool season.
examples.cn: 这里的农民在凉爽季节种萝卜和白菜。

examples.en: Grated radish is often served with grilled fish.
examples.cn: 擦碎的萝卜常和烤鱼一起吃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞的士」——萝卜脆得咬一口像招呼一辆的士；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 radix（根）→ 古英语 rædic → 古法语 radis → 英语 radish，核心义「长在地下、可挖出的根」。

sensesIntro.en: Radish starts as the root vegetable, then spreads to the edible root, the count unit, the plant, a family label, a flavour, and finally cheap or humble images.
sensesIntro.cn: radish 先指这种根菜，再扩展到可食的根、计数单位、整株植物、类名、味道，最后是便宜或质朴的联想。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crisp red-white root pulled from the soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：从土里拔出的一颗脆生红白萝卜。

branches.en: The root vegetable is the first and central meaning.
branches.cn: 根菜本身是最核心的第一个义项。

branches.en: The edible root and the count unit are so many pieces of the same vegetable.
branches.cn: 可食的根与计数单位，都是同一蔬菜的具体片段。

branches.en: The plant in the ground grows out of the vegetable meaning.
branches.cn: 地里的整株植物由蔬菜义延伸而来。

branches.en: A family label covers several look-alike root crops.
branches.cn: 类名义涵盖多种相似的根菜。

branches.en: The peppery taste is the root flavour turned into a description.
branches.cn: 辛辣味义是把根部风味变成一种描述。

intro.en: Radish is a root-named vegetable, with Latin radix and its Latin family beside it.
intro.cn: radish 是以「根」命名的蔬菜，旁边是拉丁语 radix 及其拉丁词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin radix means root, and words built on it all keep the sense of something fundamental.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 radix 意为根，由它构成的词都保留「根本」之义。

items.example: Radix names the plant organ.
items.exampleCN: radix 指植物的根部。

items.example: Radish is the vegetable word.
items.exampleCN: radish 是这种蔬菜的名称。

items.meaning: the tiny first root of a seedling
items.example: The radicle is the tiny first root.
items.exampleCN: radicle 指种子萌发的第一条细根。

items.example: The suffix -y forms radishy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 radishy。

items.example: Radishy means tasting of radish.
items.exampleCN: radishy 表示有萝卜味。

items.meaning: half the width of a circle
items.example: Radius comes from the same root.
items.exampleCN: radius 出自同一词根。

items.example: Radical literally goes to the root.
items.exampleCN: radical 字面上就是「到根上」。

items.meaningCN: 表示粗大、猛烈的组合成分
items.example: The horse- in horseradish marks a strong root.
items.exampleCN: horseradish 中的 horse- 表示根味猛烈。

items.example: Horseradish joins horse and radish.
items.exampleCN: horseradish 由 horse 与 radish 组合而成。

definition_zh: 半径；半径范围；桡骨；辐射状区域
definition_en: the distance from the centre of a circle to any point on its edge, or a similar measured distance
core_image: 圆心到圆周的一条直线，像车轮的辐条
scene: 绘图员把圆规的一只脚定在圆心，张开另一只脚，量出圆的半径。The draughtsman fixed one leg of the compass at the centre and measured a radius along the paper.
sceneCN: 这里 radius 是「半径」（第 1 个义项：圆心到圆周的距离）；句意：绘图员把圆规的一只脚定在圆心，在纸上量出一段半径。

derivatives.zh: 径向的；辐射状的：由 radius 加形容词后缀 -ial 构成，指沿半径方向的
径向地：由 radial 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
弧度：由 radius 派生，以半径为单位度量角度的数学单位
根本的；激进的：同出拉丁语 radix，与 radius 共享词根来源

senses.title: The line from centre to edge
senses.definition: the straight distance from the centre of a circle to its edge
senses.definitionCN: 从圆心到圆周上任意一点的直线距离
senses.example: The radius of this circle is ten centimetres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个圆的半径是十厘米。
senses.why: Latin radius meant a spoke or ray, and the spoke really runs from the hub to the rim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 radius 意为辐条或光线，而辐条正是从轮毂伸到轮缘，所以半径就是那根辐条。

senses.title: The plural radii in mathematics
senses.definition: a measure given for several circles at once, using the plural radii
senses.definitionCN: 同时给出多个圆的这一度量，复数写作 radii
senses.example: The two circles have radii of three and five.
senses.exampleCN: 两个圆的半径分别是三和五。
senses.why: The Latin plural radii survives because geometry borrowed the word directly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁复数 radii 得以保留，是因为几何学直接借用了这个词。

senses.title: A range of action
senses.definition: the area within which something can act, reach, or be done
senses.definitionCN: 某事物能够作用、到达或进行的范围
senses.example: The plane cannot fly beyond its radius of action.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机无法飞出它的活动半径。
senses.why: The circle around the centre becomes a practical limit: how far a plane or device can go.
senses.whyCN: 围绕中心的圆变成了实际限度：飞机或设备能走多远。

senses.title: Distance searched or covered
senses.definition: a distance set as the limit for a search or an operation
senses.definitionCN: 为搜索或行动设定的距离限度
senses.example: Police searched a three-kilometre radius around the house.
senses.exampleCN: 警方搜查了房子周围三公里的范围。
senses.why: The measured geometric distance turns into a rule for how far to look or act.
senses.whyCN: 可测量的几何距离变成了「该找多远、做到多远」的规定。

senses.title: The outer bone of the forearm
senses.definition: the shorter, thicker bone on the thumb side of the human forearm
senses.definitionCN: 人前臂拇指一侧较短的粗骨
senses.example: The fall broke his radius near the wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 那一跤摔断了他靠近手腕的桡骨。
senses.why: The bone was named for the spoke of a wheel because it turns like one at the elbow.
senses.whyCN: 这块骨因像车轮辐条那样在肘部转动而得名，于是也叫桡骨。

senses.title: A ray-like line
senses.definition: a line or spoke extending outward from a centre, as in an old word for a ray
senses.definitionCN: 从中心向外伸出的线或辐条，是表示光线的古义
senses.example: The radii of the sun wheel spread like rays.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳轮的辐条像光芒一样向外散开。
senses.why: The original Latin sense is a ray or spoke, so this shadow meaning still flickers in the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语本义就是光线或辐条，这个古义至今仍隐然存在。

senses.title: An area of near reach
senses.definition: the area close to a place, within easy reach
senses.definitionCN: 某地附近、容易到达的范围
senses.example: There are no shops within a radius of two miles.
senses.exampleCN: 两英里范围内没有商店。
senses.why: A radius around a point describes not just distance but everything close to that point.
senses.whyCN: 围绕某点的半径不仅描述距离，也描述该点附近的一切。

senses.title: A stylised circle mark
senses.definition: a circular or rounded symbol or badge marking a station or rank
senses.definitionCN: 标示车站或职级的圆形或半圆标志
senses.example: The bus stop sign carries a red circle on a blue ground.
senses.exampleCN: 公交站牌上有一个蓝底红色圆形标志。
senses.why: Because a radius often marks the edge of a circle, the word can name the rounded badge itself.
senses.whyCN: 因为半径常标出圆的边界，这个词也能指那个圆形标志本身。

senses.title: A field or zone of influence
senses.definition: the zone over which power, radiation, or effect spreads out
senses.definitionCN: 权力、辐射或作用向外扩散的领域
senses.example: The new tower serves a radius of thirty miles.
senses.exampleCN: 新塔为半径三十英里的区域提供服务。
senses.why: The circle of reach easily becomes a map of influence, from radio towers to armies.
senses.whyCN: 「可达圆圈」很容易变成一张影响地图，从广播塔到军队都用它。

intro.en: Radius is a straight Latin word for a rod, spoke, or ray of light, later borrowed by geometry.
intro.cn: radius 是拉丁语中表示杆、辐条或光线的词，后来被几何学借用。

items.en: A reconstructed root for a rod or spoke lies behind it.
items.cn: 一般认为其背后是表示杆或辐条的重构词根。

items.en: Radius means a rod, a spoke of a wheel, or a ray of light.
items.cn: 拉丁语 radius 意为杆、车轮辐条或光线。

items.en: Roman writers use radius for a surveying rod as well.
items.cn: 公元一世纪罗马作家也用 radius 指测量杆。

items.en: Geometry borrows radius for the line from centre to edge.
items.cn: 文艺复兴时期的拉丁语几何学借用 radius 表示圆心到圆周的线。

items.en: English takes radius from Latin and keeps the Latin plural radii.
items.cn: 现代英语从拉丁语引入 radius，并沿用拉丁复数 radii。

note.en: Radius is the geometric spoke-word, close in spelling to radish and radix, and near in meaning to diameter, circumference, and range.
note.cn: radius 是与「辐条」相关的几何词，拼写接近 radish、radix，意义上靠近 diameter、circumference 与 range。

entries.definition: a small root vegetable
entries.definitionCN: 萝卜：与 radius 同源自「根」，但意义完全不同，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a root or base number
entries.definitionCN: 基；根：与 radius 同出拉丁根词

entries.definition: arranged in lines from a centre
the Latin plural of radius
entries.definitionCN: radius 的拉丁语复数形式

entries.definition: broadcasting by means of waves
entries.definitionCN: 广播：与 radius 同源自光线义，但拼写相近易混

entries.definition: the distance straight across a circle
entries.definitionCN: 直径：横穿圆心的距离，正好是半径的两倍

entries.definition: the length around the edge of a circle
the area something can reach
entries.definitionCN: 范围；射程：与「活动半径」义近

normalIntro.en: Radius is the spoke of a circle: it runs from the hub to the rim, and it also names the bone that turns like a spoke.
normalIntro.cn: radius 就是圆的辐条：从轮毂伸到轮缘，也指像辐条那样转动的那块骨头。

normal.en: Radius and radix share the Latin root sense, and both describe a line coming from a centre or a base.
normal.cn: radius 与 radix 共享拉丁「根」的观念，都描述从中心或底部伸出的线。

normal.en: The Latin plural is radii, and plain English also accepts radiuses.
normal.cn: 拉丁复数写作 radii，普通的英语也接受 radiuses。

normal.en: A radius is always half the length of the diameter of the same circle.
normal.cn: 半径总是同一圆直径长度的一半。

normal.en: The radius bone lies on the thumb side of the forearm.
normal.cn: 桡骨位于前臂拇指一侧。

normal.en: In local talk, a radius means the distance within which you will search or build.
normal.cn: 在城市口语中，radius 指你会搜索或建设的距离范围。

abstract.en: Picture a wheel and one bright spoke from the hub to the metal rim.
abstract.cn: 想象一个车轮，以及一根从轮毂直伸到金属轮缘的亮辐条。

abstract.en: Draw a circle with a pin and a pencil, the string between them being the radius.
abstract.cn: 想象用图钉和铅笔绕出一圈，拉直的线就是半径。

abstract.en: Breathe out as an expanding ring, each point the same distance from the centre.
abstract.cn: 想象吐气时向外扩散的圆环，环上每一点到中心都一样远。

examples.en: Measure the radius before you cut the round board.
examples.cn: 切这块圆板之前先量一下半径。

examples.en: The blast damaged buildings within a radius of half a mile.
examples.cn: 爆炸损坏了半英里范围内的建筑。

examples.en: Students must understand the relationship between radii and diameters.
examples.cn: 学生必须理解半径与直径之间的关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞迪额斯」——像一圈很「瑞」光从中心射出；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 radius（杆、车轮辐条、光线）→ 文艺复兴几何学「圆心到圆周的线」→ 英语 radius，核心义「从中心伸出的直线」。

sensesIntro.en: Radius begins with the geometric line, takes a Latin plural, extends to reach and range, then to the forearm bone and to ray-like marks.
sensesIntro.cn: radius 从几何上的直线开始，有拉丁复数，再扩展到范围与射程，又指前臂的桡骨和射线般的标志。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bright spoke running from hub to rim.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根从轮毂伸到轮缘的亮辐条。

branches.en: The centre-to-edge line is the core geometric sense.
branches.cn: 圆心到圆周的线是核心几何义。

branches.en: The Latin plural marks the mathematical measurement as a group.
branches.cn: 拉丁复数标示数学度量的成组意义。

branches.en: Reach and search distance grow out of the circle around a centre.
branches.cn: 可达范围与搜索距离都由绕中心的圆长出。

branches.en: The forearm bone is the spoke that turns at the joint.
branches.cn: 桡骨就是关节处转动的辐条。

branches.en: A ray-like line and the nearby area keep the old spoke and ray picture.
branches.cn: 射线状线与周边范围保留了辐条与光线的旧意象。

intro.en: Radius sits in a Latin family: radius, radix, and their English children radial and radian.
intro.cn: radius 属于一个拉丁词族：radius、radix 以及英语派生出的 radial、radian。

latinIntro.en: Latin radius means a rod, spoke, or ray, and radix means root, the two being related in sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 radius 意为杆、辐条或光线，radix 意为根，二者意义相关。

items.example: Radius named a wheel spoke.
items.exampleCN: radius 原指车轮辐条。

items.example: Radius is the geometry term.
items.exampleCN: radius 是几何术语。

items.meaningCN: 辐条（复数）；半径的拉丁复数
items.example: Radii is the Latin plural.
items.exampleCN: radii 是拉丁语复数。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms radial.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 构成 radial。

items.example: Radial describes spoke-like lines.
items.exampleCN: radial 描述辐条状的线。

items.example: Radially means outward from the centre.
items.exampleCN: radially 表示从中心向外。

items.example: A radian is built on the radius.
items.exampleCN: 弧度单位建立在半径之上。

items.example: Radical shares the root word radix.
items.exampleCN: radical 与 radix 同根。

items.example: Diameter means a measure across.
items.exampleCN: diameter 意为横跨的度量。

definition_zh: 猖獗的；蔓延的；猛烈的；（纹章）后腿直立前爪高举的
definition_en: spreading quickly and in an uncontrolled way, usually of something bad
core_image: 一头野兽后腿立起、前爪狂挥，势不可挡地向前冲
scene: 城市道路上的电动车抢道之风越来越盛，居民抱怨这股乱象已经难以约束。In this city, traffic accidents caused by riders cutting lanes have become rampant in recent months.
sceneCN: 这里 rampant 是「猖獗的、失控蔓延的」（第 1 个义项：坏现象迅速蔓延而无法控制）；句意：在近几个月里，这种因抢道引发的交通事故已经变得十分猖獗。

derivatives.zh: 猖獗地；狂暴地：由 rampant 加副词后缀 -ly 构成
猖獗；蔓延：由 rampant 加名词后缀 -cy 构成，表示失控扩散的状态
猛冲；暴跳；蔓延：与 rampant 同源的动词，核心是向前冲
猛烈；蔓延：由 rampant 加名词后缀 -ness 构成

senses.title: Spreading out of control
senses.definition: spreading quickly and freely, in a way that is hard to stop, often of something bad
senses.definitionCN: 迅速而自由地传播，难以制止，多指坏事
senses.example: Disease was rampant in the crowded camp.
senses.exampleCN: 在这拥挤的营地里，疾病十分猖獗。
senses.why: Old French ramper means to crawl, and a plant or animal that crawls unchecked over everything is the picture of runaway spread.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 ramper 意为爬行，一路不受拦阻地爬满各处，正是失控蔓延的画面。

senses.title: Growing with violence
senses.definition: violent, fierce, or raging with great energy
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈、狂放、带着巨大能量的
senses.example: Rampant rumours swept through the school.
senses.exampleCN: 狂热的流言传遍了学校。
senses.why: The heraldic beast rears up and paws the air, and its wild energy became the sense of fierce force.
senses.whyCN: 纹章上的猛兽后腿立起、前爪在空中乱抓，那股狂野的力量演化成「猛烈」义。

senses.title: Reared up in heraldry
senses.definition: of an animal in a coat of arms, raising its front legs and striking out
senses.definitionCN: 纹章中的动物抬起前腿、作出扑击姿势的
senses.example: The old crest shows a rampant lion with drawn claws.
senses.exampleCN: 古老的徽章上是一头后腿直立、利爪伸出的狮子。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: a heraldic animal stands rampant when it rears up on its hind legs.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：纹章中的动物后腿立起时称为 rampant。

senses.title: Plant growth by crawling
senses.definition: growing and spreading by creeping or climbing over other things
senses.definitionCN: 通过爬行或攀附其他物体而蔓延生长
senses.example: Bindweed is a rampant grower that soon covers a fence.
senses.exampleCN: 旋花是一种蔓生植物，很快就会爬满篱笆。
senses.why: The crawling verb survives in the botanical use, where a plant creeps upward without support and spreads.
senses.whyCN: 爬行的动词义保留在植物用法中，指植物无支撑地向上爬并四散蔓延。

senses.title: Rampant in an economic sense
senses.definition: rising or increasing without control, as in prices, inflation, or debt
senses.definitionCN: 在价格、通胀或债务等方面失去控制地上涨
senses.example: Rampant inflation forced many families to cut spending.
senses.exampleCN: 恶性通货膨胀迫使许多家庭削减开支。
senses.why: Once the word meant any unchecked spread, economists picked it for numbers that grow out of control.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词泛指一切失控的扩散后，经济学家就选它来描述失控增长的数字。

senses.title: Widespread and unchecked
senses.definition: existing everywhere and going unpunished or unstopped
senses.definitionCN: 到处都存在，却无人惩处或制止
senses.example: Corruption had become rampant at every level of the office.
senses.exampleCN: 办公室里各级都已是腐败横行。
senses.why: The idea of crawling over everything turns into a moral picture: a bad habit or crime covering the whole of society.
senses.whyCN: 「爬满一切」的意象变成道德画面：坏习气或罪行覆盖了整个社会。

senses.title: An arch or curve upward
senses.definition: of a barrier or wall, rising steeply, as in architecture
senses.definitionCN: 指建筑中的矮墙或隔断陡升向上，用于建筑描述
senses.example: A low wall held the two gardens apart.
senses.exampleCN: 一道向上拱起的矮墙把两座花园隔开。
senses.why: The rear-up image lives on in architecture, where a wall rises toward the ground like a rearing arch.
senses.whyCN: 立起的意象延续在建筑术里，矮墙像弓身跃起一样陡升。

senses.title: A rearing pose in art
senses.definition: a figure or animal shown rising firmly on its hind legs
senses.definitionCN: 指人物或动物以两腿站起的腾跃姿态呈现
senses.example: The bronze horse is rampant and looks ready to jump.
senses.exampleCN: 那匹铜马后腿直立，仿佛随时要跃起。
senses.why: Art and sculpture keep the heraldic pose for its energy, so any rearing figure can be called rampant.
senses.whyCN: 艺术与雕塑为表现力量而保留纹章姿势，于是任何腾跃的形象都可用 rampant 形容。

senses.title: Rampant with pride or temper
senses.definition: of a mood, wildly fierce or without restraint
senses.definitionCN: 形容情绪极度猛烈、毫无节制
senses.example: His rampant temper drove the whole team away.
senses.exampleCN: 他狂暴的脾气把整个团队都赶走了。
senses.why: Fierce energy extends from beasts to human feelings, so a temper can be rampant too.
senses.whyCN: 猛烈的能量从野兽延伸到人的情绪，于是脾气也可以 rampant。

intro.en: Rampant comes from Old French rampant, crawling or climbing, from ramper, to creep.
intro.cn: rampant 来自古法语 rampant（爬行、攀爬），源于动词 ramper（爬）。

items.en: Franconian words for crawling and climbing lie behind it.
items.cn: 一般认为其背后是法兰克语中表示爬行、攀爬的词。

items.en: Ramper means to crawl or climb.
items.cn: 古法语 ramper 意为爬行或攀爬。

items.en: Rampant enters English, first in heraldry.
items.cn: 中古英语时期 rampant 进入英语，最初用于纹章。

items.en: Heraldic writers fix the name rampant for a beast standing on its hind legs.
items.cn: 十五世纪，纹章作者用 rampant 专称后腿立起的猛兽。

items.en: The word is applied to disease and to plant growth.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，这个词被用于疾病与植物的蔓延。

items.en: Rampant spreads to inflation, crime, and any unchecked rise.
items.cn: 二十世纪 rampant 扩展到通胀、犯罪和一切失控增长。

note.en: Rampant is the crawling word that became the queen of unchecked spread, close in spelling to rampage and ramp, and near in meaning to widespread, rife, and unrestrained.
note.cn: rampant 是从「爬行」变来的「失控蔓延」之词，拼写接近 rampage、ramp，意义上靠近 widespread、rife、unrestrained。

entries.definition: a slope, or to rush wildly
entries.definitionCN: 坡道；猛冲：与 rampant 同源，含急冲之意

entries.definition: to rush about in a violent way
entries.definitionCN: 横冲直撞：与 rampant 同源

entries.definition: a defensive wall
entries.definitionCN: 城墙；防御土墙：拼写相近，但词源与 rampant 无关，只是拼写相近

entries.definition: in an uncontrolled way
the state of spreading unchecked
found in many places
common and spreading, usually of something bad
impossible to stop or check
entries.definitionCN: 无法控制的；难以制止的

normalIntro.en: Rampant keeps the crawling image of ramper: a thing that creeps over everything and will not be stopped.
normalIntro.cn: rampant 保留了 ramper 的「爬行」意象：爬上一切、难以制止。

normal.en: A rampant lion in a crest is not lying down: it rears on its hind legs and strikes out.
normal.cn: 徽章上的狮子后腿立起、前爪挥出，而不是趴着。

normal.en: Run rampant is the everyday verb phrase for anything spreading without control.
normal.cn: run rampant 是表示「失控蔓延」的日常动词搭配。

normal.en: Rampant is almost always used for bad things: disease, crime, inflation, rumour.
normal.cn: rampant 几乎总搭配坏事：疾病、犯罪、通胀、流言。

normal.en: The adjective takes more and most, rarely rampanter.
normal.cn: 这个形容词用 more 和 most 比较，几乎不使用 rampanter。

normal.en: Rampant and ramp share the same forward rush of a veering animal.
normal.cn: rampant 与 ramp 共享一头动物急冲直撞的动势。

abstract.en: See a lion standing on its hind legs, claws slashing at the empty air.
abstract.cn: 想象一头狮子后腿立起，利爪在空中乱挥。

abstract.en: Watch a green vine creep over a fence and then over a whole house.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿藤爬过篱笆，又爬满整栋房子。

abstract.en: Hear the rumble of a stampede that is already too close to stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一群野牛奔来的轰鸣，已经近得无法阻挡。

examples.en: Rumours about the merger ran rampant through the office.
examples.cn: 关于合并的流言在办公室内四处蔓延。

examples.en: The government promised to fight rampant corruption.
examples.cn: 政府承诺打击猖獗的腐败。

examples.en: Rampant weeds had swallowed the whole garden path.
examples.cn: 疯长的杂草已经吞没了整条花园小径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「软喷」——坏消息像喷泉软软一喷就止不住地扩散；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 ramper（爬行）→ 分词 rampant（爬行的、立起的）→ 纹章中「后腿立起」的兽形 → 英语 rampant，核心义「不受控地爬满、蔓延」。

sensesIntro.en: Rampant starts in heraldry and plant growth, becomes crawling violence, then takes over disease, economy, and morals as anything that spreads unchecked.
sensesIntro.cn: rampant 从纹章与植物生长起步，转为狂烈的动势，随后在疾病、经济和道德领域普遍指一切不受控地蔓延的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a beast reared on its hind legs, clawing at everything.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头后腿立起、向四周乱抓的猛兽。

branches.en: Unchecked spread is the modern headline sense.
branches.cn: 不受控的蔓延是现代最常见的核心义。

branches.en: The reared beast supplies the sense of violence and force.
branches.cn: 立起的野兽提供猛烈与力度的义感。

branches.en: Heraldry keeps the oldest picture of the rearing animal.
branches.cn: 纹章义保留最古老的立起兽形画面。

branches.en: Plants creeping over a wall keep the crawling verb alive.
branches.cn: 植物爬上墙保留了「爬行」的动词语义。

branches.en: Inflation and corruption share the picture of a thing covering everything.
branches.cn: 通胀与腐败共享「覆盖一切」的画面。

intro.en: Rampant builds with a French root and a set of English suffixes around ramp and rampage.
intro.cn: rampant 由法语词根构成，并以 ramp、rampage 为中心形成一组英语派生词。

latinIntro.en: Rampant has no Latin ancestor; its source is Old French ramper, to crawl.
latinIntro.cn: rampant 没有拉丁语祖先，来源是古法语动词 ramper（爬行）。

items.example: Ramper gives the crawling image.
items.exampleCN: ramper 提供爬行的意象。

items.example: The suffix -ant forms rampant.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ant 构成 rampant。

items.example: Rampant is the modern adjective.
items.exampleCN: rampant 是现代形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms rampantly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 rampantly。

items.example: Rampantly means wildly.
items.exampleCN: rampantly 表示狂暴地。

items.example: The suffix -cy forms rampancy.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cy 构成 rampancy。

items.example: Rampancy names the state.
