items.exampleCN: rampancy 指猖獗状态。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms rampantness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 rampantness。

items.example: Ramp shares the French source.
items.exampleCN: ramp 与 rampant 同源。

items.example: Rampage grew from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: rampage 由同一词干发展而来。

definition_zh: 赎金；解救；给……付赎金；为……支付赎金而换回的
definition_en: money paid to free a person who is held prisoner, or the act of buying back someone or something held captive
core_image: 一笔钱递过去，门锁随即打开，被扣住的人走出来
scene: 那位绑匪留下字条，要求午夜前交出一笔钱财才肯放人。The kidnapper left a note demanding a ransom before midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 ransom 是「赎金」（第 1 个义项：为放人而支付的款项）；句意：绑匪留下一张字条，要求在午夜前交付赎金。

collocations.zh: 坚持索要赎金；要价不放

derivatives.zh: 赎人者；付赎金的人
可赎回的；可以用赎金换回的
赎金 + 软件，指锁住文件索要钱财的恶意程序

senses.title: Money paid to free a captive
senses.definition: a sum of money demanded or paid to set a prisoner free
senses.definitionCN: 为放人而被索取或支付的款项
senses.example: They paid a large ransom for the release of the sailors.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为让水手获释支付了一大笔赎金。
senses.why: The oldest sense comes from the Latin redemptio, a buying back, so the sum of money is literally the price of return.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项来自拉丁语 redemptio（买回），所以赎金就是「把人换回来」的价钱。

senses.title: The act of setting a captive free
senses.definition: the act of freeing a prisoner or captive in exchange for payment
senses.definitionCN: 用付款交换俘虏或人质自由的行为
senses.example: His ransom was arranged by a distant cousin.
senses.exampleCN: 他的获释是由一位远房表亲张罗的。
senses.why: Since the money and the freeing happen together, the noun can also name the whole transaction of release.
senses.whyCN: 付钱与放人总是同时发生，所以名词也可以指整个「赎人」的过程。

senses.title: To buy someone freedom
senses.definition: to pay money so that a prisoner or captive can go free
senses.definitionCN: 付钱使被关押者或俘虏获得自由
senses.example: The villagers ransomed the boy from his captors.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们向绑匪付钱赎回了那个男孩。
senses.why: The noun became a verb in the fifteenth century, and the action simply repeats the money-for-freedom bargain.
senses.whyCN: 名词在十五世纪转成动词，动作就是重演「以钱换自由」的那笔交易。

senses.title: Torment for payment
senses.definition: the crime of holding a person and demanding money for their release
senses.definitionCN: 扣押他人并索要钱财才放人的罪行
senses.example: Ransom has become a serious problem along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 绑架勒索已成为沿海地区的一个严重问题。
senses.why: Used without an article, the word names a whole criminal practice, not one payment.
senses.whyCN: 不带冠词单独使用的时候，这个词指一整类犯罪行为，而不是某一笔钱。

senses.title: A price for release
senses.definition: a price or condition paid to regain something valuable that was taken
senses.definitionCN: 为重新获得被夺走之物而付出的价格或条件
senses.example: The old city paid a ransom of silver to keep its walls standing.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古城为保住城墙，交出了作为代价的白银。
senses.why: When what is held back is a place or a treasure rather than a person, the ransom becomes a general price of release.
senses.whyCN: 被扣住的对象从人扩展到城池或宝物时，赎金就泛化为「换取放行的代价」。

senses.title: Something redeemed
senses.definition: a person or thing that has been bought back or set free
senses.definitionCN: 被赎回或释放的人或物
senses.example: The freed hostages were called the ransom of the long war.
senses.exampleCN: 获释的人质被称为那场漫长战争赎回的成果。
senses.why: Old religious writing used the noun for the saved soul, turning the payment into the thing recovered.
senses.whyCN: 古老的宗教文本用这个词指获救的灵魂，于是赎金又从「付出之物」转成了「被救回之物」。

intro.en: Ransom goes back through Old French rançon to Latin redemptio, a buying back, from redimere, to buy back.
intro.cn: ransom 经古法语 rançon 上溯到拉丁语 redemptio（买回），源于 redimere（赎回）。

items.en: Redimere, built on re- back and emere to buy, means to buy back.
items.cn: redimere 由 re-（回）与 emere（买）构成，意为买回。

items.en: Redemptio means a buying back or a ransom.
items.cn: redemptio 意为买回或赎身。

items.en: Rançon carries the buying-back idea into French.
items.cn: rançon 把「买回」的概念带入法语。

items.en: Ransom first appears in Middle English for money paid to free a captive.
items.cn: ransom 最早见于中古英语，指为释放俘虏而付的钱。

items.en: The noun is used as a verb, to ransom a prisoner.
items.cn: 名词被用作动词，表示赎回俘虏。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to ransom notes and ransom payments.
items.cn: 现代英语进一步扩展出索赎字条与赎金支付等说法。

note.en: Ransom shares the Latin buy-back root with redemption and redeemer, and sits beside ordinary words for paying for release.
note.cn: ransom 与 redemption、redeemer 共享拉丁语「买回」词根，并与表示「付钱放人」的常用词相邻。

entries.definition: to buy back or regain possession of something
the act of buying something back
a person who buys back or saves another
malicious software that locks files until money is paid
entries.definitionCN: 锁定文件直到付费才解锁的恶意软件

entries.definition: a person held captive until demands are met
a person who is kept in a prison or a cage
to take a person away illegally and hold them
the crime of demanding money by using threats

normalIntro.en: Ransom keeps the Latin picture of buying a person back, and the word family around it makes the price of freedom visible.
normalIntro.cn: ransom 保留了拉丁语「把人买回来」的画面，同族词则把自由的价钱摆到眼前。

normal.en: The Latin verb redimere pairs re- back with emere to buy, and ransomers pay exactly that return price.
normal.cn: 拉丁语动词 redimere 由 re-（回）与 emere（买）组成，而付赎金的人付的正是这笔「买回去」的价钱。

normal.en: The Old French rançon dropped the d of redemptio, which is how the English r appeared.
normal.cn: 古法语 rançon 丢掉了 redemptio 里的 d，英语里 r 开头的拼写就是这样来的。

normal.en: To hold somebody for ransom is a fixed phrase: the holding and the demand always travel together.
normal.cn: hold somebody for ransom 是固定说法：扣人与索钱总是绑在一起的。

normal.en: Ransom note and ransom demand mark the criminal side, while redeem marks the religious sense of rescue.
normal.cn: ransom note 与 ransom demand 指向犯罪层面，而 redeem 更常用于宗教意义上的救赎。

normal.en: Ransomware is a modern coinage: the same demand for money, this time aimed at computer files.
normal.cn: ransomware 是现代新造词：同样是索钱，只不过这次盯上的是电脑文件。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed envelope of coins sliding across a table, and a key sliding back.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的钱袋从桌面滑过去，钥匙从另一边滑回来。

abstract.en: Imagine a heavy door opening only after the right sum is counted out.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇沉重的门，只有数对金额之后才会打开。

abstract.en: See a hand paying, and a young face walking free into daylight.
abstract.cn: 看见一只手在付款，一张年轻的脸走进日光里获得自由。

examples.en: The gang demanded a million pounds in ransom.
examples.cn: 该团伙索要一百万英镑的赎金。

examples.en: Priests once ransomed prisoners taken in border raids.
examples.cn: 过去，神职人员曾出资赎出在边境突袭中被俘的人。

examples.en: No country should have to pay for the return of its own citizens.
examples.cn: 任何国家都不该为自己公民的获释付钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「人丧命，钱赎人」——钱财一到手，被扣的人就能脱身；这只是谐音拆分联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 redimere（re- 回 + emere 买，意为买回）→ 拉丁语 redemptio（买回；赎身）→ 古法语 rançon → 中古英语 ransoun → 英语 ransom，核心义「以钱把人买回来」。

sensesIntro.en: Ransom begins with money paid to free a captive, then names the act of release and the verb, and finally widens to the crime and to any price of return.
sensesIntro.cn: ransom 先指为放人而付的钱，再指赎人的行为与动词用法，最后扩展到绑架勒索以及任何「换回」的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pays a sum, and a locked door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手付出一笔钱，锁着的门随之打开。

branches.en: The money itself is the central sense.
branches.cn: 赎金本身是核心义项。

branches.en: The act of release and the verb grow from the same moment of payment.
branches.cn: 放人的行为与动词用法都出自付款那一刻。

branches.en: Used as a practice, the word names kidnapping for money.
branches.cn: 当作一类行为时，这个词指绑架索财。

branches.en: A captured town or treasure can also command a price for release.
branches.cn: 被扣的城池或宝物同样可以用来换取放行代价。

branches.en: The buyer and the bought-back person sit on the two sides of one bargain.
branches.cn: 付款者与被赎回者处在同一笔交易的两端。

intro.en: Ransom is a whole word borrowed through French, and its Latin parts re- and emere explain why it has always meant buying back.
intro.cn: ransom 是经法语整体借入的词，它内部的拉丁成分 re- 与 emere 解释了为什么它一直表示「买回」。

latinIntro.en: Latin redimere joins re- back with emere to buy, and redemptio names the buying back itself.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 redimere 由 re-（回）与 emere（买）组合而成，redemptio 则指买回这一行为。

items.example: Redimere gives the whole word its buying-back image.
items.exampleCN: redimere 为整个词提供「买回」的意象。

items.example: Redemptio is the direct ancestor of the word.
items.exampleCN: redemptio 是这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: Rançon is the French form that English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: rançon 是英语借入的法语形式。

items.example: The prefix re- signals that something comes back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 表示某物回到原处。

items.example: Emere is the buying part of the root.
items.exampleCN: emere 是词根中「买」的那一半。

items.meaning: having a quality; not part of ransom
items.meaningCN: 具有某性质（与 ransom 无关）
items.example: The -some of handsome is a suffix, but the -som of ransom is not.
items.exampleCN: handsome 里的 -some 是词尾，但 ransom 里的 -som 不是。

items.meaning: a person who pays a ransom
items.example: Ransomer adds the person suffix -er.
items.exampleCN: ransomer 由表示人的后缀 -er 构成。

items.example: Redeem comes from the same Latin verb, without the French step.
items.exampleCN: redeem 来自同一个拉丁动词，只是没经过法语这一站。

items.example: Redemption is the Latin noun brought in unchanged.
items.exampleCN: redemption 是原样借入的拉丁名词。

items.example: Ransomware joins ransom with ware, meaning goods.
items.exampleCN: ransomware 由 ransom 与 ware（物品）复合而成。

definition_zh: 敲击；叩击声；说唱音乐；说唱；厉声责备；指控；快速地说
definition_en: a sharp quick knock, the fast rhyming music called rap, or a sharp criticism or criminal charge
core_image: 指节在木门上急速叩三下，发出短促而干脆的响声
scene: 裁判敲了两下木槌，随后念出对他的正式指控。The referee rapped twice on the table, then read out the formal charge.
sceneCN: 这里 rap 是「叩击」（第 1 个义项：短促快速的敲打）；句意：裁判在桌上敲了两下，随后念出正式指控。

derivatives.zh: rap + -er（人），指说唱歌手
现在分词转名词，指说唱这种表演形式
全神贯注的；入迷的（来自拉丁语 raptus，只是拼写相近，词源不同）

senses.title: A sharp quick knock
senses.definition: a sudden short hard hit, especially with the knuckles on a door
senses.definitionCN: 突然短促用力的一击，尤指用指节敲门
senses.example: There was a sharp rap on the window.
senses.exampleCN: 窗上传来一声短促的敲击。
senses.why: The word is imitative: it copies the dry sound of knuckles or a stick hitting wood.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是拟声词，模仿指节或木棍敲在木头上的干脆声响。

senses.title: To strike quickly and hard
senses.definition: to hit something quickly and firmly, often with a small object
senses.definitionCN: 快速而用力地敲打某物，常使用小物件
senses.example: She rapped the table with her pen to call for silence.
senses.exampleCN: 她用笔敲桌子，要求大家安静。
senses.why: The sound and the action are one thing, so the noun easily became a verb of striking.
senses.whyCN: 声音与动作本是一回事，所以名词很自然地转变为表示敲击的动词。

senses.title: A style of rhyming music
senses.definition: a style of music in which words are spoken in rhythm over a beat
senses.definitionCN: 在有节拍的伴奏上按节奏念词的音乐形式
senses.example: Rap grew out of the streets of New York in the seventies.
senses.exampleCN: 说唱乐于七十年代在纽约街头兴起。
senses.why: The words are delivered like rapid taps on the beat, so the knock image fits the style.
senses.whyCN: 唱词像一连串急促的敲点在节拍上落下，因此「敲击」的画面正好贴合这种音乐。

senses.title: A sharp public reprimand
senses.definition: a strong criticism or scolding given quickly and sharply
senses.definitionCN: 快速而严厉的批评或斥责
senses.example: The coach rapped the team for being late again.
senses.exampleCN: 教练严厉批评全队又一次迟到。
senses.why: Just as a rap is quick and hard, a spoken rap is a sharp hit with words.
senses.whyCN: 正如敲击又快又重，言语上的敲打就是用词语重重地打一下。

senses.title: A criminal charge
senses.definition: an official accusation of a crime, especially in informal American speech
senses.definitionCN: 正式的犯罪指控，尤其在美式口语中使用
senses.example: He has a rap sheet from years ago.
senses.exampleCN: 他多年前就有一份犯罪记录。
senses.why: The sense comes from taking the rap, because a charge lands on a person like a blow.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自承担责任的说法，因为指控落到某人身上就像一记敲打。

senses.title: To rap out a command
senses.definition: to say something quickly in a sharp or forceful voice
senses.definitionCN: 用尖锐有力的声音快速说出某事
senses.example: The officer rapped out a list of names.
senses.exampleCN: 警官急促地念出一串名字。
senses.why: Each syllable falls like a tap, so speaking fast and sharply is described as rapping out.
senses.whyCN: 每个音节都像一下敲点，所以又快又重地说出就被说成敲出来。

intro.en: Rap is usually taken as an imitative word for a sharp blow or knock; scholars relate it to Middle Low German and Dutch rappen, to strike.
intro.cn: rap 一般认为由拟声而来，指短促的一击；学者多把它与中古低地德语和荷兰语 rappen（打击）相联系。

items.en: A reconstructed imitative root for a quick tap is often proposed but is uncertain.
items.cn: 常有人提出一个表示「快敲」的拟声重构词根，但这一说法并不确定。

items.en: Rap first appears in Middle English as a blow or a knock.
items.cn: rap 最早的记录见于中古英语，指一击或敲打。

items.en: Slang uses take the rap and beat the rap, referring to blame and charges.
items.cn: 十八世纪的俚语出现承担责任与脱罪的说法，与责备和指控有关。

items.en: In the United States rap comes to mean rapid rhyming speech.
items.cn: 二十世纪六七十年代的美式英语中，rap 开始指快速押韵的念词。

items.en: Modern English uses rap for the music, the performer and the style.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rap 指这种音乐、表演者与风格。

note.en: Rap is a short imitative word, easily confused in spelling with wrap and rapt, and close in meaning to knock, tap and charge.
note.cn: rap 是简短的拟声词，拼写容易与 wrap、rapt 混淆，含义上则与 knock、tap、charge 等词相邻。

entries.definition: to cover something in paper or cloth
entries.definitionCN: 包；裹（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: so interested that you give all your attention
entries.definitionCN: 全神贯注的（来自拉丁语，只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a person who performs rap music
the act of speaking rhymes over a beat
to hit a door or surface to attract attention
to hit something lightly and quickly
an official statement accusing someone of a crime
to speak angrily to someone about their behaviour

normalIntro.en: Rap is one syllable that sounds like what it names: a quick, dry tap on a hard surface.
normalIntro.cn: rap 只有一个音节，听起来就像它所指的事：硬表面上一下干脆的敲击。

normal.en: The short syllable rap imitates a knock, which is why the noun and the verb look identical.
normal.cn: rap 这个短音节模仿敲击声，所以名词和动词拼写完全相同。

normal.en: Past tense is rapped with a double p, just like stopped and planned.
normal.cn: 过去式是 rapped，双写 p，和 stopped、planned 的变化规则一样。

normal.en: Take the rap means to accept the blame, as if a charge lands on you as a blow.
normal.cn: take the rap 意为承担罪责，仿佛指控像一击落在你身上。

normal.en: Do not confuse rap with wrap: wrap has a silent w and means to cover.
normal.cn: 别把 rap 和 wrap 搞混：wrap 多一个不发音的 w，意思是包裹。

normal.en: A rap on the knuckles is a light punishment, so the knock became a metaphor for correction.
normal.cn: a rap on the knuckles 指轻微处罚，于是敲打又引伸为惩戒的比喻。

abstract.en: Hear three hard taps on a wooden door in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 在安静的房间里，听见木门上三下硬实的敲击。

abstract.en: Picture a judge bringing down a gavel, and each tap is a small judgment.
abstract.cn: 想象法官落槌，每一下敲击都是一次小小的判决。

abstract.en: Follow a beat where the singer spits words like stones against a wall.
abstract.cn: 跟着一段节奏，唱歌的人把词一个字一个字像石子一样甩到墙上。

examples.en: Someone rapped loudly on the back door.
examples.cn: 有人大声敲了敲后门。

examples.en: He took the rap for a mistake that was not his.
examples.cn: 他为一个不属于自己的错误背了黑锅。

examples.en: The programme gives young people free access to the recording studio.
examples.cn: 这个项目让年轻人免费使用录音棚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉普」——想象一首曲子只「拉」起节拍「普」普通通地念词，就是敲着拍子说唱；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为拟声来源，模仿短促的一击；可能与中古低地德语、荷兰语 rappen（击打）同源，词源存疑。核心义「短促敲击」→「说唱」→「厉声责备 / 指控」。

sensesIntro.en: Rap starts as the sound and act of a hard quick knock, then extends to rap music, to sharp blame, to a criminal charge and to speaking fast and sharply.
sensesIntro.cn: rap 起初是硬朗快速的敲击声与敲击动作，再扩展到说唱音乐、厉声责备、刑事指控以及急促地说话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three quick taps of knuckles on a wooden door.
core.cn: 核心意象：指节在木门上急速叩三下。

branches.en: The sound of the tap is the first sense.
branches.cn: 敲击的声音与动作是第一义项。

branches.en: Hitting a surface is the verb that follows from the noun.
branches.cn: 敲打表面的动词由名词直接引申而来。

branches.en: Words tapped out on a beat become rap music.
branches.cn: 在节拍上敲出来的词就成了说唱音乐。

branches.en: A sharp rap with words is a scolding, and rapid delivery is rapping out.
branches.cn: 用词语重敲一下就是责备，快速吐出则说成急促地念出。

branches.en: A charge that lands on someone is the legal version of the blow.
branches.cn: 落在某人身上的指控是敲击在法律层面的版本。

intro.en: Rap is a short native word with no Latin parts, and its family is built with the noun and person suffixes.
intro.cn: rap 是简短的英语本族词，不含拉丁成分，它的词族靠名词与人名后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Rap is imitative rather than Latin in origin, so the Latin side is limited to later borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: rap 来源为拟声而非拉丁语，因此拉丁语一面仅限于后来的借入成分。

items.meaning: the act of knocking or performing rap
items.example: Rapping comes from the verb with the suffix -ing.
items.exampleCN: rapping 由动词加后缀 -ing 构成。

items.example: The suffix -er turns rap into rapper.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 把 rap 变成 rapper。

items.example: Rapper is the everyday person noun for the music.
items.exampleCN: rapper 是这种音乐最常用的人称名词。

items.example: Rapped doubles the p before -ed.
items.exampleCN: rapped 在 -ed 前双写 p。

items.example: Rap sheet keeps the charge sense in slang.
items.exampleCN: rap sheet 在俚语中保留了指控义。

items.meaningCN: 包裹（形近词，无词源关系）
items.example: Wrap has a silent w and a different history.
items.exampleCN: wrap 有一个不发音的 w，来历也不同。

items.meaningCN: 入迷的（形近词，源自拉丁语）
items.example: Rapt comes from Latin raptus, not from rap.
items.exampleCN: rapt 来自拉丁语 raptus，与 rap 无关。

items.meaningCN: 快速的（形近词，源自拉丁语）
items.example: Rapid only shares a few letters with rap.
items.exampleCN: rapid 只与 rap 共享几个字母。

items.example: Knock is the ordinary word that rap echoes.
items.exampleCN: knock 是 rap 所呼应的普通日常词。

definition_zh: 狂喜；极度喜悦；着迷；入迷
definition_en: a feeling of extreme pleasure and joy, or the state of being carried away by strong emotion
core_image: 抬头望天，整个人被一股喜悦托起，脚几乎离开地面
scene: 演出结束的那一刻，全场观众陷入一片狂喜，久久不肯离场。The moment the show ended, the whole audience rose in rapture and refused to leave.
sceneCN: 这里 rapture 是「狂喜」（第 1 个义项：极度的喜悦）；句意：演出结束的那一刻，全场观众陷入狂喜，迟迟不肯离场。

derivatives.zh: rapture 去掉名词词尾 -ure，指全神贯注、入迷的
rapture 加 -ous，表示「欣喜若狂的；热烈的」
由 rapturous 加 -ly 构成，义为「狂热地；欣喜万分地」
en-（使进入）+ rapture，义为「使欣喜若狂」

senses.title: A feeling of overwhelming joy
senses.definition: a feeling of intense delight that seems to lift a person out of themselves
senses.definitionCN: 强烈到仿佛把人托出自身的喜悦感
senses.example: She stared at the newly opened flower in rapture.
senses.exampleCN: 她欣喜若狂地凝视着那朵刚刚绽放的花。
senses.why: Latin raptus means seized and carried off, so rapture is joy that snatches a person away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 raptus 意为被攫走、被带走，所以狂喜就是一种把人掳走的喜悦。

senses.title: A state of being spellbound
senses.definition: a state in which someone is so absorbed that they seem elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 完全沉浸其中、仿佛灵魂在其他地方的状态
senses.example: The children watched the magician with rapture.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们入迷地看着魔术师。
senses.why: If joy carries a person away, the resulting trance is the same carrying-away seen from inside.
senses.whyCN: 如果喜悦把人带走，那么随之而来的出神状态就是从内部看同一场「被带走」。

senses.title: A burst of enthusiasm
senses.definition: an outburst of great praise or excitement about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物的极度赞美或兴奋的爆发
senses.example: Critics went into raptures over her first novel.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家对她的第一部小说赞不绝口。
senses.why: The plural turns a private feeling into a public shout of praise, so raptures name excited talk.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式把私人的感受变成公开的赞美，于是说 raptures 就指激动的夸赞。

senses.title: Union with the divine
senses.definition: in religious writing, the lifting of the soul toward God
senses.definitionCN: 宗教文本中指灵魂向神飞升的状态
senses.example: The old painting shows a saint caught up in rapture.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅古画描绘了一位圣人神魂超拔的一幕。
senses.why: Religious writers used raptus for a soul seized by God, which gives rapture its heavenly sense.
senses.whyCN: 宗教作者用 raptus 表示灵魂被神攫取，这赋予 rapture 一种升向天上的意味。

senses.title: Being carried off in an older sense
senses.definition: in older texts, the act of carrying someone or something away
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文本中，指将人或物带走的行为
senses.example: The chronicle records the rapture of the town by the raiders.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史记载了劫掠者掳走该镇人口一事。
senses.why: Before it meant joy, the word simply named a seizure, and a few formal texts keep that meaning alive.
senses.whyCN: 在表示喜悦之前，这个词只表示「攫夺」，少数正式文本仍保留这一含义。

intro.en: Rapture comes from Latin raptus, a seizing, and rapere, to seize, through medieval Latin raptura.
intro.cn: rapture 来自拉丁语 raptus（攫取）与 rapere（抓住），经由中世纪拉丁语 raptura 进入英语。

items.en: Rapere means to seize or carry off by force.
items.cn: rapere 意为用力抓取或掳走。

items.en: Raptus names the act of seizing and the state of being seized.
items.cn: raptus 既指抓取的动作，也指被攫住的状态。

items.en: Raptura refers to a carrying off, especially of the soul toward God.
items.cn: raptura 指被带走，尤指灵魂向神飞升。

items.en: Rapture arrives in English first in the religious sense of ecstatic seizure.
items.cn: rapture 进入英语时首先用于宗教意义，指神魂被攫。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word widens to excellent joy and to enchantment.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词扩展到极度的喜悦与着迷。

note.en: Rapture belongs to the Latin seize family of rapere, near in form to rapt and rapturous, and near in meaning to ecstasy and delight.
note.cn: rapture 属于拉丁语 rapere（抓取）词族，形式上接近 rapt、rapturous，含义上接近 ecstasy、delight。

entries.definition: so interested that you give all your attention
showing great delight and excitement
to fill someone with great delight
a close friendly relationship
entries.definitionCN: 融洽的关系（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a feeling of extreme happiness
great pleasure
perfect happiness
a feeling of intense excitement and happiness

normalIntro.en: Rapture is built on the Latin rapere, to seize, so the word keeps a picture of someone caught up and carried away by joy.
normalIntro.cn: rapture 建立在拉丁语 rapere（抓取）之上，因此这个词始终保留着「被喜悦攫走带走」的画面。

normal.en: Latin rapere means to seize, so rapture is joy that seizes a person.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 rapere 意为抓取，所以 rapture 是抓走一个人的喜悦。

normal.en: The abstract noun suffix -ure turns the seized state into a name, as in measure and departure.
normal.cn: 抽象名词后缀 -ure 把「被攫住」的状态变成名词，就像 measure 和 departure 那样。

normal.en: Rapt is the short adjective for being spellbound, and it shares the Latin past participle.
normal.cn: rapt 是表示入迷的短形容词，与词源共享同一个拉丁语过去分词。

normal.en: Rapturous adds -ous to mean full of rapture, as in danger and dangerous.
normal.cn: rapturous 加 -ous 表示「充满狂喜的」，就像 danger 与 dangerous 的关系。

normal.en: The usual pattern is in rapture or go into raptures over something.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 in rapture 与 go into raptures over something。

abstract.en: Picture a face lifted to a bright sky, feet still on the floor but barely.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸仰向明亮的天空，脚还贴着地面，却几乎要离开。

abstract.en: Imagine a theatre audience holding its breath, not wanting the moment to end.
abstract.cn: 想象剧场里的观众屏住呼吸，不愿意这一刻结束。

abstract.en: See someone staring at a flame so closely that the room disappears.
abstract.cn: 看见有人紧盯着火焰，整个房间仿佛都消失了。

examples.en: The children listened to the story in rapture.
examples.cn: 孩子们入迷地听着故事。

examples.en: The visitors stood in rapture before the frozen waterfall.
examples.cn: 游客们站在冰封的瀑布前，欣喜若狂。

examples.en: The play drew rapturous notices from every critic.
examples.cn: 这部戏赢得了评论家们欣喜若狂的好评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「热扑千」——心里热得扑上来一千个欢呼，就是狂喜；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rapere（抓取、掳走）→ raptus（被攫住的状态）→ 中世纪拉丁语 raptura → 英语 rapture，核心义「被喜悦攫走」。

sensesIntro.en: Rapture starts with a feeling of overwhelming joy, moves to the spellbound state it creates, then to loud praise and to the older religious and literal senses.
sensesIntro.cn: rapture 先指压得人喘不过气的喜悦，再指由此产生的入迷状态，然后扩展到热烈的赞美，以及更早的宗教义与字面义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person lifted by joy, feet barely touching the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被喜悦托起，双脚几乎离开地面。

branches.en: Overwhelming joy is the modern core sense.
branches.cn: 压倒一切的喜悦是现代的核心义项。

branches.en: Being spellbound is the state that joy produces.
branches.cn: 入迷出神是喜悦带来的状态。

branches.en: Public praise is the social form of the same feeling.
branches.cn: 公开的赞美是同一种感受在社交场合的形态。

branches.en: The religious sense keeps the original rising movement.
branches.cn: 宗教义保留了原本向上飞升的动势。

branches.en: The oldest literal sense still shows the seized object.
branches.cn: 最早的抓取含义仍显露出被夺走之物。

intro.en: Rapture is a Latin noun in -ure built on rapere, and its family includes rapt, rapturous and enrapture.
intro.cn: rapture 是由拉丁语 rapere 加上 -ure 构成的名词，词族包括 rapt、rapturous 与 enrapture。

latinIntro.en: Latin rapere means to seize, raptus means seized, and raptura names the carrying away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rapere 意为抓取，raptus 意为被攫住，raptura 指被带走这件事。

items.example: Rapere supplies the seizing image.
items.exampleCN: rapere 提供「攫取」的意象。

items.example: Raptus underlies the adjective rapt.
items.exampleCN: raptus 是形容词 rapt 的来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ure makes a noun of action, as in departure.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ure 构成表示动作的名词，如 departure。

items.example: Rapt keeps the past participle of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: rapt 保留了拉丁语动词的过去分词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms rapturous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成 rapturous。

items.example: Rapturous describes loud, joyful praise.
items.exampleCN: rapturous 形容热烈而喜悦的赞美。

items.example: The prefix en- forms enrapture.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 构成 enrapture。

items.example: Enrapture is the verb built on rapture.
items.exampleCN: enrapture 是在 rapture 基础上构成的动词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms rapturously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 rapturously。

items.example: Rapturously tells how the crowd cheered.
items.exampleCN: rapturously 说明人群如何欢呼。

items.example: Raptures is the plural used in go into raptures.
items.exampleCN: raptures 是复数形式，用于 go into raptures。

items.meaningCN: 快速的（形近词，源自拉丁语 rapidus）
items.example: Rapid shares the root rapere but means swift, not ecstatic.
items.exampleCN: rapid 与它同源于 rapere，但意思是迅速，而非狂喜。

definition_zh: 稀薄化；变稀薄的过程；稀疏化；稀薄区；稀疏状态
definition_en: the process or result of making something less dense, especially air or sound energy in a wave
core_image: 一间小屋里的空气被慢慢抽走，四壁向外鼓起
scene: 物理课上老师拨动音叉，演示声音在空气里怎样一疏一密地传开。In the physics class the teacher struck a tuning fork to show how a sound wave reaches our ears through rarefaction and compression.
sceneCN: 这里 rarefaction 是「稀疏化」（第 1 个义项：气体或物质变稀薄的过程）；句意：物理课上老师敲响音叉，演示声音通过空气的稀疏与压缩传到我们耳中。

derivatives.zh: 由 -faction 反推出同族动词，义为「使变稀薄；使稀疏」
由 rarefy 加 -ed 构成，义为「稀薄的；脱离大众的」
由 -faction 换形容词后缀 -ive，义为「导致稀薄的」
由 rarefy 加 -able 构成，义为「可变稀薄的」

senses.title: The process of becoming thin
senses.definition: the process of making a gas or other substance less dense
senses.definitionCN: 使气体或其他物质密度降低的过程
senses.example: Rarefaction of the air near the summit makes breathing hard.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶附近空气稀薄，让人呼吸困难。
senses.why: Latin facere means to make, so rarefaction names the act of making air more rare.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 facere 意为「做、使」，所以 rarefaction 指的是把空气变得更稀薄这一动作。

senses.title: A thin patch in a sound wave
senses.definition: the region of a sound wave where the medium is stretched and less dense
senses.definitionCN: 声波中介质被拉伸、密度较低的区段
senses.example: Compression and rarefaction alternate as the wave travels.
senses.exampleCN: 波在传播时，压缩区与稀薄区交替出现。
senses.why: Because the noun names the making thin, it also labels the stretched part of the wave.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词本指「变稀」的过程，于是也用来指波中被拉伸的那一段。

senses.title: A state of sparse sparseness
senses.definition: the condition of being thinly spread or scattered
senses.definitionCN: 分布稀疏、零散的状态
senses.example: The rarefaction of the crowd left the square quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 人群变得稀疏，广场上安静下来。
senses.why: The making-thin action is extended to any set of things that becomes thinly spread.
senses.whyCN: 「变稀」的动作可以推广到任何变得稀疏的事物集合。

senses.title: An act of refinement
senses.definition: the act of refining or making something purer and more refined
senses.definitionCN: 提炼、使事物更纯净或更精致的行为
senses.example: The rarefaction of dining turned a meal into a ritual.
senses.exampleCN: 用餐饮的精致化把一顿饭变成了一种仪式。
senses.why: Latin purus, pure, hides in rarefaction, so clearing away dross became a metaphor for refinement.
senses.whyCN: rarefaction 里藏着拉丁语 purus（纯净），因此去掉杂质也就引申为「精致化」。

senses.title: Heightened inner life
senses.definition: a spiritual or emotional state described as elevated, in older devotional use
senses.definitionCN: 旧时宗教文本中形容受提升的精神或情感状态
senses.example: The writer spoke of a rarefaction of the soul in prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 作者谈到祈祷时灵魂的一种升华。
senses.why: Old devotional prose borrowed the chemical sense for the soul made finer by grace.
senses.whyCN: 旧时宗教散文借用化学上的「提纯」义，形容灵魂因恩典而变得更精微。

intro.en: Rarefaction combines Latin rarus, thinly spread, with facere, to make, and purus, clean, and arrived in English through early modern scientific Latin.
intro.cn: rarefaction 由拉丁语 rarus（稀疏）结合 facere（做、使）与 purus（纯净）构成，经近代早期的科学拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: Rarus means thinly spread or uncommon, and it is the anchor of the whole family.
items.cn: rarus 意为分布稀疏或不常见，是整个词族的核心。

items.en: Rarefieri means to become rare, and rarefacere means to make rare, built on facere.
items.cn: rare fieri 意为「变稀薄」，rarefacere 意为「使稀薄」，后者建立在 facere 之上。

items.en: The noun rarefactio, sometimes written with purus rather than rarus, names a reduction of density.
items.cn: 名词 rarefactio 有时写作 purus 而非 rarus，指密度的降低。

items.en: Early modern scientific Latin fixes rarefaction as the standard term for air and gas becoming thin.
items.cn: 近代早期科学拉丁语把 rarefaction 固定为空气或气体变稀薄的标准术语。

items.en: English natural philosophers adopt the word for experiments on thin air and sound.
items.cn: 十七世纪英国自然哲学家把该词用于稀薄空气与声音的实验。

items.en: Modern English extends it to sparse crowds, refined art, and religious elevation.
items.cn: 现代英语又把它扩展到稀疏的人群、精致的艺术与宗教上的升华。

note.en: Rarefaction sits with the rare family and next to words for density and thinning.
note.cn: rarefaction 属于 rare 词族，又紧邻表示密度与变稀的词。

entries.definition: to make or become less dense
thin in air or refined in tone
the state of being uncommon
the amount of mass in a given space
the squeezing of a gas into a smaller space
the quality of being thin or sparse

normalIntro.en: Rarefaction is rare plus a making suffix: the process of turning something into rarefied or thin matter.
normalIntro.cn: rarefaction 由 rare 加表示「使……化」的后缀组成：把某物变成稀薄状态的过程。

normal.en: Rarefaction and compression come in pairs in every sound wave.
normal.cn: 每个声波里，稀疏与压缩都是成对出现的。

normal.en: The rarefaction of the air on the mountain makes breathing hard.
normal.cn: 山上空气的稀薄化让人呼吸困难。

normal.en: Rarefy is the verb, and rarefied the adjective, from the same stem.
normal.cn: 同词干的动词是 rarefy，形容词是 rarefied。

normal.en: A rarefaction wave is the stretch that follows a shock.
normal.cn: rarefaction wave 指冲击之后出现的那道拉伸。

normal.en: Compare rarify, a less common spelling that some dictionaries still list.
normal.cn: 对比 rarify：这是一种较少见的拼写形式，有些词典仍然收录。

abstract.en: Picture an invisible hand pulling the air molecules apart.
abstract.cn: 想象一只隐形的手把空气分子彼此拉开。

abstract.en: See a slinky stretched in one spot and squeezed in the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一只弹簧被拉长一处、又压紧一处。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd on a beach spreading out into empty sand.
abstract.cn: 想象沙滩上的人群散开，露出大片空沙。

examples.en: The rarefaction of the air at altitude slows the climbers.
examples.cn: 高处的空气稀薄，拖慢了登山者的步伐。

examples.en: Scientists measure rarefaction caused by heat in a sealed tube.
examples.cn: 科学家测量密封管中由热引起的稀薄化。

examples.en: A sound wave carries a rarefaction wave behind each crest.
examples.cn: 声波在每个波峰之后都带着一段稀疏波。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「锐儿开克申」——把气压锐减、「开」出一条稀疏的空隙，正是变稀薄；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rarus（稀疏、罕见）+ facere（做、使）→ 拉丁语 rarefacere（使稀薄）与名词 rarefactio → 近代科学拉丁语 rarefaction → 英语 rarefaction，核心义「使变稀薄的过程」；该词形里有时混入 purus（纯净）的形式。

sensesIntro.en: Rarefaction begins with the physical thinning of air, moves to the thin part of sound waves, and then spreads to sparse crowds, refined taste, and elevated spirit.
sensesIntro.cn: rarefaction 先从空气物理上的变稀薄出发，转到声波里的稀薄区，再扩展到稀疏的人群、精致的品味与升华的精神。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air being pulled apart in a closed room.
core.cn: 核心意象：密闭房间里被抽得越来越薄的空气。

branches.en: The concrete physical process is the base sense.
branches.cn: 具体物理过程是基础义项。

branches.en: The stretched part of a wave is the acoustics sense.
branches.cn: 波中被拉伸的一段是声学义项。

branches.en: Any scattered set can be described as in rarefaction.
branches.cn: 任何变得零星散开的集合都能用稀疏来描写。

branches.en: Refinement and spiritual elevation are metaphors of thinning toward purity.
branches.cn: 精致化与精神升华都是朝纯净「变稀」的比喻。

branches.en: A sound wave only exists because air alternates between density and rarefaction.
branches.cn: 声波之所以存在，正因为空气在压缩与稀薄之间来回交替。

intro.en: Rarefaction is a compound noun joining rarus, thin, with facere, to make, and its English family reaches rarefy and rarefied.
intro.cn: rarefaction 是把 rarus（稀疏）与 facere（使）合成的名词，它的英语词族延伸到 rarefy 与 rarefied。

latinIntro.en: Latin rarus means thinly spread, facere means to make, and purus means pure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rarus 意为稀疏，facere 意为做、使，purus 意为纯净。

items.example: Rarus gives the family its thin image.
items.exampleCN: rarus 提供「稀疏」的意象。

items.example: Facere adds the idea of making.
items.exampleCN: facere 补上「使……成为」的意思。

items.example: Rarefacere is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: rarefacere 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: The suffix -faction turns a verb into a noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -faction 把动词变成表示过程的名词。

items.example: Rarefaction keeps the scientific sense.
items.exampleCN: rarefaction 保留了科学含义。

items.example: Rarefy is the common English verb.
items.exampleCN: rarefy 是常见的英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms rarefied.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 rarefied。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms rarefactive.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 构成 rarefactive。

items.example: Purus survives in one spelling of the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: purus 留在该拉丁名词的一种拼写里。

definition_zh: 稀有；罕见；珍贵少见的状态；稀薄
definition_en: the quality or state of being rare, uncommon, or thinly occurring
core_image: 一片枯叶躺在满地的落叶里，几乎没人注意到它
scene: 博物馆里那枚邮票被单独放在玻璃柜中央，游人都在它面前停下脚步。Visitors stopped at the cabinet because the rareness of the stamp made it worth the long queue.
sceneCN: 这里 rareness 是「稀有、珍贵少见的状态」（第 2 个义项：某物因不常见而珍贵）；句意：游客们在展柜前停下，因为这枚邮票的稀有让它值得排长队。

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，后加 -ness 构成 rareness，义为「稀有的；罕见的」
由 rare 加 -ly 构成，义为「很少；难得」
同一词根换成 -ity 后缀的名词，义为「稀有；珍品」，比 rareness 更常用
由 rare 加比较级后缀 -er 构成，义为「更稀有的」

senses.title: The quality of being uncommon
senses.definition: the quality of occurring seldom or not often being found
senses.definitionCN: 很少发生或很少被找到的性质
senses.example: The rareness of the bird makes it hard to study.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟十分罕见，因此很难研究。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns the adjective rare into the abstract quality of being uncommon.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ness 把形容词 rare 变成「不常见」这一抽象性质。

senses.title: Preciousness of a scarce thing
senses.definition: the preciousness that comes from scarcity in the world of collectors
senses.definitionCN: 收藏圈里因稀缺而带来的珍贵性
senses.example: Collectors pay dearly for the rareness of early coins.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏家为早期钱币的珍稀付出高价。
senses.why: Scarcity feeds value, so the quality of being rare also names the preciousness it carries.
senses.whyCN: 稀缺会带来价值，所以「稀有」这种性质也指它附带的珍贵。

senses.title: Thinness of the air
senses.definition: the thinness or low density of a gas such as air
senses.definitionCN: 空气等气体的稀薄或低密度
senses.example: Rareness of the air at high altitude tires hikers.
senses.exampleCN: 高海拔空气稀薄，让徒步者感到疲惫。
senses.why: Rare also describes thinly spread air, and the noun inherits that physical thinness.
senses.whyCN: rare 也形容分布稀疏的空气，名词因此继承了这种物理上的稀薄。

senses.title: Sparseness of occurrence
senses.definition: a low rate at which an event happens
senses.definitionCN: 某个事件发生的低频率
senses.example: The rareness of such storms makes them hard to predict.
senses.exampleCN: 这类风暴十分稀少，因此难以预测。
senses.why: The same quality applies to events counted over time rather than to found objects.
senses.whyCN: 同一种性质也可以用于按时间计数的「事件」，而不只用于被找到的物品。

senses.title: A rare instance
senses.definition: a rare thing or case itself, viewed as a single rare item
senses.definitionCN: 稀有之物或罕见的事例本身
senses.example: The rarenesses of the archive are locked away.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆里的稀有之物都被锁了起来。
senses.why: The abstract quality can be turned back into a countable thing that carries it.

intro.en: Rareness is formed in English from rare plus the native suffix -ness, replacing the older rarity in some uses.
intro.cn: rareness 是在英语内部由 rare 加本族后缀 -ness 构成的，在某些用法中取代了较早的 rarity。

items.en: Rarus means thinly spread, sparse, or uncommon.
items.cn: rarus 意为分布稀疏、稀少或不常见。

items.cn: 古法语把这一形容词借为 rare，再传给英语。

items.en: Rare settles in English for uncommon things and thin air.
items.cn: rare 在英语中固定下来，用于罕见之物与稀薄空气。

items.en: The suffix -ness, inherited from Old English -nes, forms nouns of quality.
items.cn: 后缀 -ness 继承自古英语 -nes，用来构成表示性质的名词。

items.en: Rareness stays close to the root rare, while rarity is the more common noun.
items.cn: rareness 更贴近词根 rare，而 rarity 才是更常用的名词。

note.en: Rareness is a plain -ness noun beside rare, rarely, and rarer, and it overlaps with rarity.
note.cn: rareness 是紧邻 rare、rarely、rarer 的 -ness 型名词，与 rarity 意义重叠。

normal.en: Rareness and rarity mean almost the same, but rarity is far more common.

normal.en: The suffix -ness builds nouns of quality, as in kindness and darkness.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ness 构成表示性质的名词，如 kindness 与 darkness。

normal.en: Rarely is the adverb, and rareness is the matching noun.

normal.en: The rareness of a sighting is what makes birdwatchers travel far.

normal.en: Use rareness when the sentence needs a plain state noun, not a collectible.
normal.cn: 需要朴素的「状态名词」而非「藏品」时，用 rareness。

abstract.en: Picture one white feather in a field of black ones.
abstract.cn: 想象一片黑色羽毛中只夹着一根白色的。

abstract.en: Imagine a price tag that climbs each time an object is harder to find.
abstract.cn: 想象一件东西越难找到，价格标签就越高。

abstract.en: Think of a mountain trail where the air gets thinner with every step.
abstract.cn: 想象一条山道，每走一步空气就更薄一点。

examples.en: The rareness of clean wells worries the villagers.

sensesIntro.en: Rareness first names the state of being uncommon, then the preciousness of scarce goods, then puts that quality back on objects, events, and thin air.
sensesIntro.cn: rareness 先指「不常见的状态」，再指稀缺之物的珍贵，随后又把这种性质落回物品、事件与稀薄空气上。

branches.en: Scarcity turned into value is the collectors sense.
branches.cn: 稀缺变成价值，是收藏圈义项。

branches.en: The physical thinness of gas is the inherited sense.
branches.cn: 气体的物理稀薄是继承来的义项。

branches.en: Events counted over time and rare things themselves both carry the quality.
branches.cn: 按时间计数的事件与稀有之物本身都承载这种性质。

branches.en: A thing is both uncommon and valuable, which is why rareness sells.
branches.cn: 一件东西既不常见又珍贵，所以「稀有」能卖钱。

definition_zh: 稀有；罕见；珍品；稀薄
definition_en: the state of being uncommon, or an item that is seldom found and highly valued
core_image: 黑色丝绒上一颗只此一枚的宝石，四周留出大片空白
scene: 拍卖师戴着手套取出一枚旧币，举高让全场看清，随后报出一个令人屏息的价格。The auctioneer called the old coin a true rarity and watched the room fall silent.
sceneCN: 这里 rarity 是「珍品」（第 2 个义项：因罕见而珍贵的东西）；句意：拍卖师称这枚旧币是真正的珍品，看着全场安静下来。

senses.title: The state of being uncommon
senses.definition: the state of not being common or not occurring often
senses.definitionCN: 不常见或很少发生的状态
senses.example: The rarity of the pollen makes it hard to collect.
senses.exampleCN: 这种花粉十分稀有，难以采集。
senses.why: Latin -itas forms nouns of state, so rarity names the condition of being rarus, uncommon.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -itas 构成表示状态的名词，rarity 因此指「不常见」这一状态。

senses.title: A precious rare thing
senses.definition: an object that is seldom found and therefore highly valued
senses.definitionCN: 因极少见到而价值很高的物品
senses.example: This stamp is a rarity that every collector wants.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚邮票是人人都想收藏的珍品。
senses.why: A quality can turn into a countable thing, so rarity also labels the rare item itself.
senses.whyCN: 性质可以转指承载它的可数之物，所以 rarity 也指稀罕的物品本身。

senses.title: Thinness of air
senses.definition: the low density of the air at high altitude
senses.definitionCN: 高海拔处空气的低密度
senses.example: The rarity of the mountain air tired the team.
senses.exampleCN: 山里空气稀薄，让队伍感到疲惫。
senses.why: Rarus also meant thinly spread, so the same noun covers thin as opposed to dense air.
senses.whyCN: rarus 也意为分布稀疏，所以同一个名词也能指稀薄而非浓密的空气。

senses.title: An exceptional event
senses.definition: an unusual occurrence that happens only occasionally
senses.definitionCN: 只偶尔发生的不寻常事件
senses.example: Snow in the desert is a rarity.
senses.exampleCN: 沙漠下雪是一件罕见的事。
senses.why: The state sense extends to events, so an event of that state is itself a rarity.
senses.whyCN: 状态义项也用于事件，于是处于这种状态的事件本身就成了「罕见之事」。

senses.title: Thin, refined quality
senses.definition: a refined, subtle quality in air, sound, or style
senses.definitionCN: 空气、声音或风格中精致微妙的品质
senses.example: Critics praised the rarity of the prose.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这篇散文的精微。
senses.why: Thin matter can become mere airy refinement, so rarity also praises delicate quality.
senses.whyCN: 稀薄的物质可以变成近乎空灵的精微，因此 rarity 也用来称赞细腻的品质。

definition_zh: 正式批准；追认（尤指条约、宪法修正案等经法定程序确认生效）
definition_en: the formal act of giving official approval to an agreement, treaty, or constitutional change so that it becomes legally valid
core_image: 一枚印章落在条约末尾的签名旁，原本悬着不定的约定就此定下
scene: 国际会议上，一百多位代表依次在气候协定上签字，但协定还需各国议会点头才能生效。The treaty took effect three months after the final ratification by the last member state.
sceneCN: 这里 ratification 是「正式批准」（第 1 个义项：条约、协定等经法定程序获得正式认可的过程）；句意为最后一批成员国完成批准后的第三个月，条约正式生效。

pos.zh: 名词：正式批准；追认（文件、条约、修正案等的法定确认）

derivatives.zh: 正式批准；追认（动词，构成名词的根）
尚未批准的（un- 否定 + 过去分词）
批准者；批准方（-er 表示施动的人或机构）

senses.title: The formal legal act of approval
senses.definition: the official legal act by which an authority or state confirms an agreement or document and makes it binding
senses.definitionCN: 权威机构或国家以法定程序确认某项协议或文件并使它具备约束力的行为
senses.example: The ratification of the treaty required a two-thirds majority in parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 批准该条约需要议会三分之二多数通过。
senses.why: The Latin base ratifies a decision, and -ation names the act, so the word names the official confirmation itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根表示「使确认」，加上 -ation 构成表示动作的名词，所以这个词直接指「核准」这一正式行为。

senses.title: The document that records approval
senses.definition: the written instrument or document that records and transmits an official approval
senses.definitionCN: 记录并传达正式批准意见的书面文件或文书
senses.example: The ambassadors exchanged instruments of ratification in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 各国大使在首都交换了批准书。
senses.why: Because -ation can name the result of an act as well as the act, a ratification also means the paper that carries the approval.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -ation 既可指行为也可指行为的结果，所以 ratification 也指承载批准意见的那份文书。

senses.title: Retroactive endorsement of an earlier act
senses.definition: the act of giving approval after something has already been done, so that it is treated as valid
senses.definitionCN: 对已经发生的行为事后给予认可，使之被视为有效
senses.example: The board met to discuss the ratification of the manager s earlier decision.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会开会讨论对经理先前决定的追认。
senses.why: If official approval can settle a pending promise, it can also close the gap behind the person who acted early.
senses.whyCN: 既然正式批准能让悬着的承诺落定，它同样能补上「先斩后奏」留下的缺口。

senses.title: Confirming a constitutional amendment
senses.definition: the process by which states or legislatures approve an amendment so that it can come into force
senses.definitionCN: 各州或立法机构对修正案作出认可、使其得以生效的过程
senses.example: State ratification of the amendment was completed within two years.
senses.exampleCN: 各州对该修正案的批准在两年内完成。
senses.why: When the rule being confirmed is part of the constitution, the confirming act becomes a fixed step in the legal procedure.
senses.whyCN: 当被确认的对象是宪法条文时，这个核准动作就固定成了法律程序中的一道必经步骤。

senses.title: Social or collective endorsement
senses.titleCN: 社会层面的认可；集体背书
senses.definition: a public or collective acceptance that makes a practice, idea, or plan official in a social rather than legal way
senses.definitionCN: 公开或集体的接受，使某种做法、观念或计划在社会意义上而非法律意义上获得正式地位
senses.example: The festival won wide ratification from local residents and businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆获得了当地居民与商家的广泛认可。
senses.why: The same image of stamping an agreement travels outward: any group can put its collective weight behind what was provisional.
senses.whyCN: 在协议上盖章的意象可以向外延伸：任何群体都能为原本不确定的事物投下集体分量。

intro.en: Ratification is the Latin-derived noun of ratify, built on the Latin root ratus, meaning settled or confirmed. The exact first English date differs between dictionaries, so the centuries below are approximate.
intro.cn: ratification 是由 ratify 派生出的拉丁语系名词，词根为拉丁语 ratus（已定的、已确认的）。英语首见年代各家词典标注不一，下面所标世纪均为大致估计。

items.en: The core is Latin ratus, the past participle of reri, to think or judge, meaning settled, fixed, or confirmed. The root carries the idea of a decision made firm by judgement.
items.cn: 核心是拉丁语 ratus，即 reri（思考、判断）的过去分词，意为已定的、已确认的。词根带着「经判断而定下来」的意味。

items.en: Added to facere, to make, the root produced ratificare, to make settled, and the noun ratificatio, the act of making something firm or confirmed.
items.cn: 与 facere（做、使）结合成为 ratificare（使之确定），并派生出名词 ratificatio（使之确定的行为）。

items.en: In medieval legal Latin, ratificatio is used for the formal approval of an act already done by someone else, which is the ancestor of the modern legal use.
items.cn: 在中世纪法律拉丁语中，ratificatio 用于表示对他人已经作出的行为予以正式认可，这是现代法律用法的直接来源。

items.en: English takes ratify first and then ratification in the following century, applied to charters, treaties, and royal acts. The first English date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语先借入动词 ratify，随后一个世纪才出现名词 ratification，用于特许状、条约与王室行为。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: With the growth of written treaties, ratification becomes the standard word for a state confirming an agreement so that it binds the signatories.
items.cn: 随着成文条约的增多，ratification 成为国家确认协议、使之约束签约方的标准用语。

items.en: Written constitutions give ratification a fixed procedural meaning: amendments and treaties take effect only after the required number of states approve them.
items.cn: 成文宪法让 ratification 有了固定的程序含义：修正案与条约须在足够数目的州批准之后才能生效。

note.en: Ratification belongs to a small family built on ratify, and it sits close to everyday approval words and to the related act of endorsing something already done.
note.cn: ratification 属于围绕 ratify 构成的小词族，它在语义上靠近日常的「同意」类词，也靠近「追认既有行为」这一类相关动作。

official permission for an action

normalIntro.en: Ratification is the noun form of ratify, and both parts point back to the Latin root for a decision made firm.
normalIntro.cn: ratification 是 ratify 的名词形式，两者都指回拉丁语中「把决定定下来」的词根。

normal.en: Think of ratify plus -ation: the verb describes the approval, the noun names the whole act.
normal.cn: 把 ratify 加上 -ation 来看：动词描述批准动作，名词命名整个批准行为。

normal.en: Ratification of the treaty is one of the most frequent legal collocations.
normal.cn: ratification of the treaty（条约批准）是最常见的法律搭配之一。

normal.en: If a deal is subject to ratification, it is not final until the approval comes.
normal.cn: 若协议 subject to ratification（须经批准），在批准到来之前都不算定局。

normal.en: Compare approval: approval is general and everyday, while ratification is formal and usually legal.
normal.cn: 对比 approval：approval 是一般日常的赞同，ratification 则正式且多为法律程序。

normal.en: The related word ratifier identifies the body that approves, such as a parliament or a state.
normal.cn: 相关的 ratifier 指批准的一方，比如议会或国家。

abstract.en: Picture a final stamp pressing onto a long treaty in a dim hall.
abstract.cn: 想象昏暗大厅里，一枚印章最后压到长长的条约上。

abstract.en: Imagine a stack of instruments of ratification carried in an official briefcase.
abstract.cn: 想象一只公文包里装着一叠批准书。

abstract.en: See a manager signing a paper backdated to cover a decision made without permission.
abstract.cn: 想象经理在文书上补签，为一次未经许可的决定追认。

examples.en: The new trade agreement is awaiting ratification by both parliaments.
examples.cn: 这项新的贸易协定正等待两国议会批准。

examples.en: Without ratification, the proposal remains only a promise on paper.
examples.cn: 没有正式批准，这份提案就只是纸上的承诺。

examples.en: Delegates signed the charter on Monday, and ratification is expected next spring.
examples.cn: 代表们在周一签署了宪章，预计明年春天完成批准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rat + ification」——把文件像逮住耗子一样一把「摁住」并盖章，就是正式批准；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ratus（已定的、已确认的，reri「判断」的过去分词）+ facere（使）→ ratificare（使之确定）→ ratificatio → 英语 ratify / ratification，核心义「把决定定下来、盖章确认」。

sensesIntro.en: Ratification starts from the legal act of making an agreement official, then extends to the document that records it, to late approval of something already done, to constitutional procedure, and finally to social endorsement.
sensesIntro.cn: ratification 从「以法定程序使协议正式生效」这一动作出发，继而指记载批准的文书，再指对已完成之事的追认、宪法修正案的批准程序，最后扩展到社会层面的集体认可。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamp pressed onto the end of a signed treaty, making it final.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚印章盖在已签字的条约末尾，使它最终生效。

branches.en: The legal act of approval is the centre of the word.
branches.cn: 法定批准这一行为是这个词的核心义项。

branches.en: The paper that carries the approval is named with the same noun.
branches.cn: 承载批准意见的那份文书用同一个名词来表示。

branches.en: Approval given after the event is an extension of the same setting of a decision firm.
branches.cn: 事后的追认，是「把决定定下来」这一动作在时间上的延伸。

branches.en: A treaty and a constitutional amendment follow the same formal confirming procedure.
branches.cn: 条约与宪法修正案走的是同一种正式确认程序。

branches.en: Legal stamping and social endorsement both turn something provisional into something accepted.
branches.cn: 法律意义上的盖章与社会意义上的认可，都在把暂定之物变成被接受之物。

intro.en: Ratification is built from the Latin root of judgement plus a making verb and an action-noun suffix, and the whole word family may share an obscure link with ratio, reason.
intro.cn: ratification 由拉丁语「判断」词根、表示「使」的动词和表示动作的名词后缀共同构成；整个词族可能与 ratio（理由、比例）有词源关联，但这条线索并不清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin ratus means settled or confirmed, facere means to make, and -atio turns the making verb into the name of the act.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ratus 意为已定的、已确认的，facere 意为做、使，-atio 则把动词变成表示动作的名词。

definition_zh: 正式批准；核准；追认（签名或盖章使约定生效）
definition_en: to give formal and official approval to an agreement, document, or decision so that it becomes binding
core_image: 签名之后补上一枚红色的印章，让约定从「说好了」变成「定下了」
scene: 议会大厅里，议员们就一项边境条约投票，赞成票刚过半数，议长随即宣布结果。Parliament voted to ratify the border treaty by a narrow margin.
sceneCN: 这里 ratify 是「正式批准」（第 1 个义项：以法定程序确认条约或协议并使其生效）；句意为议会以微弱多数票表决批准了这项边境条约。

pos.zh: 动词：正式批准；核准；追认

senses.title: To approve a treaty or agreement formally
senses.definition: to give official approval to a treaty or agreement through the required legal procedure
senses.definitionCN: 通过法定程序对条约或协议给予正式认可
senses.example: The government needs a majority in parliament to ratify the convention.
senses.exampleCN: 政府需要议会多数票才能批准这项公约。
senses.why: The Latin base means to make settled, so ratifying a treaty is officially setting a signed promise firm.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「使之确定」，所以 ratify 条约就是把已签字的承诺正式钉死下来。

senses.title: To confirm a document or title
senses.definition: to give a document or title its official validity so that it can be relied on
senses.definitionCN: 赋予文件或称号官方有效性，使其可以被信赖使用
senses.example: The council ratified the new charter in a brief ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 议会在一次简短的仪式上核准了新的章程。
senses.why: The same stamping image applies to any piece of paper: approval turns a draft into something others must respect.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「盖章」意象适用于任何纸面文件：认可让草稿变成别人必须承认的东西。

senses.title: To endorse an act already done
senses.definition: to approve an action after it has already been taken so that it is treated as valid
senses.definitionCN: 对已经采取的行动事后加以认可，使之被视为有效
senses.example: The committee ratified the spending that had already been approved hastily.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会追认了那笔匆匆批准的支出。
senses.why: A decision is not always made in advance, and ratifying it later closes the gap behind the action.
senses.whyCN: 决定并非总在事前作出，事后 ratify 就补上了行为背后那道授权缺口。

senses.title: To make a procedure or decision binding
senses.titleCN: 确认生效；使具有约束力
senses.definition: to make a rule, decision, or procedure legally binding rather than merely intended
senses.definitionCN: 使规则、决定或程序具有法律约束力，而不再只是意向
senses.example: The states must ratify the amendment before it can take effect.
senses.exampleCN: 各州必须批准该修正案，它才能生效。
senses.why: Since the root means making firm, the strongest meaning is the one that gives a text the power to bind people.
senses.whyCN: 既然词根意为「使之坚固」，最强的含义就是赋予文本约束人的力量。

senses.title: To confirm something by witnessing
senses.definition: to confirm or witness the validity of something so that it can be accepted as genuine
senses.definitionCN: 确认或见证某事物的有效性，使其可以被承认为真实
senses.example: Two officials signed to ratify the copy of the ancient contract.
senses.exampleCN: 两位官员签字确认了这份古老合同的副本。
senses.why: Long before modern states, ratification was a witness act: a second party made another person promise firm.
senses.whyCN: 在国家出现之前，ratify 就是见证行为：由第二方把另一人的承诺固定下来。

intro.en: Ratify comes through Old French from the Latin verb ratificare, built on ratus, a participle of reri, to judge. Dictionaries disagree on the exact first English date, so the labels below are approximate.
intro.cn: ratify 经古法语来自拉丁语动词 ratificare，其词根是 reri（判断）的分词 ratus。各家词典对英语首见年代的标注不一致，下面的时代标签皆为大致估计。

items.en: Latin reri means to think, reckon, or judge, and its participle ratus means settled, fixed, or confirmed by judgement.
items.cn: 拉丁语 reri 意为思考、盘算、判断，其分词 ratus 意为经判断而确定、固定下来的。

items.en: With facere, to make, Latin formed ratificare, to make settled or to confirm, and the action noun ratificatio.
items.cn: 与 facere（使、做）结合，拉丁语构成 ratificare（使之确定、确认）及其动作名词 ratificatio。

items.en: In medieval legal records, ratificare is common in the sense of approving what another person has done, a usage that still survives today.
items.cn: 在中世纪的法律文献中，ratificare 常表示认可他人已做之事，这一用法至今仍在。

items.en: Old French ratefier or ratifier carries the verb toward English, keeping the legal colour of a confirmed decision.
items.cn: 古法语 ratefier（或 ratifier）把这个动词带向英语，也保留了「决定获确认」的法律色彩。

items.en: English ratify appears in the 14th century in legal and administrative texts. The first recorded date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 ratify 在十四世纪的法律与行政文本中已出现，但确切的最早记录年代不确定。

items.en: In modern diplomacy and constitutional law, ratify is the standard verb for a state or legislature making a treaty or amendment binding.
items.cn: 在现代外交与宪法实践中，ratify 成为国家或立法机构使条约或修正案生效的标准动词。

note.en: Ratify is a formal legal verb surrounded by its own noun family and by near synonyms of a much softer register.
note.cn: ratify 是一个正式的法律动词，身边围绕着自己的名词家族，以及一批语气温和得多的近义词。

definition_zh: 配给量；定额；口粮；（用复数）军粮；配给；定量供应
definition_en: a fixed amount of food or supplies that each person is allowed, especially when goods are scarce, or to limit how much someone can have
core_image: 手掌大小的罐头与一小袋面粉，被均匀分进每人的饭盒
scene: 地震过后，运进小镇的粮食只剩很少，仓库门口排起长队，每人只能领到手心那样一小份。Each family received a daily ration of rice and one bottle of water.
sceneCN: 这里 ration 是「配给量」（第 1 个义项：在物资紧张时按规定发给每人的一份定量）；句意为每户每天领到一份定量的大米和一瓶水。

pos.zh: 名词：配给量；定额；口粮；（复数）军粮
动词：配给；定量供应；节制使用

collocations.zh: 把某物分配给……（每份定额）

derivatives.zh: 比率；比例（同源名词，义偏「算出来的关系」）
理性的；合理的（同源形容词，义偏「符合计算」）
理由；原理（同源名词，与 ration 读音极近）
