senses.title: A fixed share of food or supplies
senses.definition: the amount of food or goods officially allowed to one person for a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 规定在一段时间内发给每人的食物或物资数量
senses.example: Each prisoner receives a shared ration of bread twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 每个囚犯每天领取两次定量的面包。
senses.why: The Latin root means reckoning or share, so a ration is the share that has been calculated and handed out by rule.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「计算、份额」，所以 ration 就是按规矩算好并分出去的那一份。

senses.title: The act of distributing limited goods
senses.definition: the system or act of limiting and distributing scarce goods in fixed amounts
senses.definitionCN: 在物资短缺时按定量限制并分发物资的制度或行为
senses.example: Wartime rationing changed what families ate for breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 战时的配给制度改变了各家餐桌上的早餐。
senses.why: When the calculated share becomes a policy, the word moves from the portion itself to the whole distributing practice.
senses.whyCN: 当算好的份额上升为一种制度时，这个词就从「那份东西」转向「分发这件事」。

senses.title: Military allowance and provisions
senses.definition: the regular allowance of food or pay given to soldiers in service
senses.definitionCN: 发给现役士兵的定期口粮或津贴
senses.example: The sergeant doled out the soldiers rations before the march.
senses.exampleCN: 行军之前，中士给士兵们分发了口粮。
senses.why: The strict calculating sense suits armies, where every man gets the amount the quartermaster has counted out.
senses.whyCN: 严格的「算好份额」义很适合军队，每个士兵都拿到军需官数好的那一份。

senses.title: To limit consumption
senses.definition: to use or give only a small, set amount so that supply lasts longer
senses.definitionCN: 只使用或只给出很少的固定量，以延长供应
senses.example: You should ration your energy during the first half of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 你应该在比赛前半程节制体力。
senses.why: The counting behind a ration becomes a verb: to ration something is to apply the same calculation to time or energy.
senses.whyCN: 配给背后的「算一算」变成了动词：对时间或精力也同样按定额来分配。

senses.title: The portion each person gets figuratively
senses.definition: the share of something abstract that is allotted to a person, such as the day allotted to work
senses.definitionCN: 分给某人的抽象份额，例如一天中被划给工作的时间
senses.example: A fair ration of sleep is part of good training.
senses.exampleCN: 足够的睡眠是良好训练的一部分。
senses.why: Once the idea is a calculated share, it can be applied to sleep, luck, or praise as easily as to bread.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个概念成为「算出来的份额」，它就能用在睡眠、运气或称赞上，和用在面包上一样自然。

intro.en: Ration goes back through Old French to Latin ratio, a reckoning or reason. The senses split away from the related word ratio, which kept the arithmetical idea, while ration kept the food portion and the military allowance. Exact first dates are uncertain.
intro.cn: ration 经古法语上溯至拉丁语 ratio（计算、理由）。它和同源词 ratio 分家：ratio 保留了算术义，ration 则保留了食物份额与军粮义。确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Latin reor, to reckon or think, gives the noun ratio, a reckoning, reason, or account. The root image is counting something out.
items.cn: 拉丁语 reor（计算、思考）给出名词 ratio，意为计算、理由、账目。词根意象就是「算一算、分一分」。

items.en: In medieval Latin, ratio also covers a fixed measure or allowance, especially in accounts of soldiers and households.
items.cn: 在中世纪拉丁语中，ratio 也指固定的份额或定量，常见于记载士兵与家用的账目中。

items.en: Old French raison keeps the sense of reason and also the measured allowance, which English later borrowed.
items.cn: 古法语 raison 既保留「理由」义，也保留按量配给的份额义，英语后来借入了后者。

items.en: English ration is used in the 17c chiefly for the daily allowance of food given to soldiers and sailors.
items.cn: 英语 ration 在十七世纪主要指令士兵与水兵每日领取的食物定量。

items.en: The world wars bring ration books and rationing into everyday life, and the word moves into civilian use for household supplies.
items.cn: 两次世界大战把配给簿与定量供应带进日常生活，这个词也进入平民家庭的物资用语。

note.en: Ration shares the Latin reckoning root with ratio and rational, and it answers to near-meaning words about shares and limits.
note.cn: ration 与 ratio、rational 同出拉丁语「计算」词根，同时在语义上靠近一批表示「份额、限量」的相近词。

entries.definition: the relation in number between two amounts
entries.definitionCN: 比率；比例，与 ration 同出拉丁语 ratio，但义偏「算出来的关系」

entries.definition: based on reason rather than feeling
entries.definitionCN: 理性的；合理的，是同一词根的形容词

entries.definition: the set of reasons behind something
entries.definitionCN: 理由；原理（同源名词，读音与拼写都极近）

entries.definition: an amount of something that is allowed
entries.definitionCN: 定额；津贴（侧重「被允许多少」）

entries.definition: a part of a larger amount given to one person
entries.definitionCN: 一份；份额（侧重从整体中分出的一部分）

entries.definition: a part of something that belongs to one person
entries.definitionCN: 份额；一份（最日常的分法说法）

normalIntro.en: Ration keeps the Latin sense of counting something out, so every meaning centres on a share fixed by calculation.
normalIntro.cn: ration 保留了拉丁语「数着分出去」的意思，所以每个含义都围绕「按计算定好的份额」。

normal.en: The verb ration out means to distribute in counted portions.
normal.cn: 动词搭配 ration out 指按数好的份额分发。

normal.en: Food rations are the fixed food allowance of a soldier or refugee.
normal.cn: food rations 指士兵或难民约定的定量食物。

normal.en: The past participle rationed appears in gas rationed during a crisis.
normal.cn: 过去分词 rationed 见于危机期间「实行配给」的汽油。

normal.en: Compare ratio and rational: they share the reckoning root, but ratio is a number and rational is a way of thinking.
normal.cn: 对比 ratio 与 rational：它们共享「计算」词根，但 ratio 是数字，rational 是思维方式。

normal.en: Teachers sometimes use the word for a small portion of attention, as in a ration of praise.
normal.cn: 老师有时也用这个词指一点点注意力，比如「分摊到的赞美」。

abstract.en: See a queue of people each holding a small tin can with the same weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一队人，每人手里的罐头重量都一样。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk cutting a loaf into equal slices and counting them out.
abstract.cn: 想象店员把面包切成等份，一片片数着发。

abstract.en: Imagine a runner glancing at a gauge that marks how much energy is left.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者在看一只标着剩余能量的表。

examples.en: During the drought, each household was given a strict ration of water.
examples.cn: 干旱期间，每户都领到严格定量的水。

examples.en: The camp rationed the medicines so that every patient got a share.
examples.cn: 营地对药品实行配给，让每位病人都能分到一份。

examples.en: Doctors advised him to ration his salt and sugar carefully.
examples.cn: 医生建议他仔细控制盐和糖的用量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rash + en」——物资紧张时不能仓促（rash）乱花，只能按「份额」发放；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ratio（计算、账目、理由，源于 reor「计算、思考」）→ 古法语 raison（理由；定额）→ 中古英语 ration，核心义「按计算分好的一份」，后由此发展出军粮、配给制度与动词「限量」。

sensesIntro.en: Ration begins with the calculated food share, extends to the rationing system and military provisions, then to the verb of limiting use, and finally to abstract shares of time or energy.
sensesIntro.cn: ration 从「算好的那份口粮」出发，扩展到配给制度与军粮，再转为「限量使用」的动词，最后用于时间、精力等抽象份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand-sized tin and a small bag of flour counted into each bowl.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小罐食物和一小袋面粉，被数着分进每个人的饭盒。

branches.en: The fixed share per person is the most basic meaning.
branches.cn: 每人一份的定量是最基本的含义。

branches.en: When the share becomes official policy, the word names the whole system of distribution.
branches.cn: 当份额上升为官方政策，这个词就指整套分发制度。

branches.en: Army provisions are the historical home of the counted share.
branches.cn: 军粮是这种「数好份额」用法最早的家园。

branches.en: The noun share and the verb of limiting use come from the same calculation.
branches.cn: 名词的份额与动词的限量，来自同一种计算。

branches.en: The counted portion applies to abstract things like time and sleep as well.
branches.cn: 数好的那份同样可以用于时间、睡眠这类抽象事物。

intro.en: Ration has no English affix of its own: it is the Latin reckoning noun arriving almost whole, with ratio, rational, and rationale grown beside it from the same root.
intro.cn: ration 本身没有英文词缀，它是几乎原样借入的拉丁语「计算」名词，身边还从同一词根长出了 ratio、rational 与 rationale。

latinIntro.en: Latin reor means to reckon; ratio means a reckoning, account, or reason. English -tion forms then build the family around it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 reor 意为计算、盘算；ratio 意为计算、账目、理由。英语的 -tion 类后缀再围绕它构成词族。

items.example: Ratio is the direct source of ration.
items.exampleCN: ratio 是 ration 的直接来源。

items.example: Reor supplies the counting image.
items.exampleCN: reor 提供「计算」意象。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -tion appears in ration and rationing forms.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -tion 见于 ration 与 rationing 这类构词中。

items.example: The suffix -al builds rational from ratio.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 由 ratio 构成 rational。

items.example: Ratio keeps the arithmetic side of the root.
items.exampleCN: ratio 保留了词根的算术一面。

items.example: The ending -nal appears in rational and rationale.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -nal 见于 rational 与 rationale。

items.example: Rationed is formed with the -ed ending.
items.exampleCN: rationed 由 -ed 词尾构成。

items.example: Rationing is built with the -ing ending.
items.exampleCN: rationing 由 -ing 词尾构成。

definition_zh: 使陶醉；使狂喜；使着迷；劫掠；掳走
definition_en: to fill someone with intense delight, or, in older use, to seize and carry something off by force
core_image: 一个人被眼前的美猛地抓住，站在原地动弹不得
scene: 她第一次听这支乐团的现场演奏，整个人被震撼得说不出话。At her first live concert the orchestra ravished her senses with one long surge of sound.
sceneCN: 这里 ravish 是「使陶醉」（第 1 个义项：用强烈的美或快乐把人的心抓住）；句意：她第一次听现场音乐会时，乐团的演奏用一浪接一浪的声音使她沉醉。

pos.zh: 劫掠；掳走；强夺（古旧用法）

collocations.zh: 使感官极度愉悦；令人陶醉
令双眼陶醉；美得让人移不开眼

derivatives.zh: 由 ravish 加 -ing 构成分词形容词，义为「令人陶醉的；美得惊人的」
由 ravishing 加 -ly 构成，义为「迷人地；美得令人倾倒地」
由 ravish 加 -ment 构成的名词，义为「陶醉；狂喜；劫掠」
由 ravish 加 -er 构成，指「抢劫者；强夺者」，古旧用法中亦指「令人沉醉者」

senses.title: To fill with intense delight
senses.definition: to fill someone with such intense pleasure that they seem to lose themselves
senses.definitionCN: 用极其强烈的愉快把某人充满，使其仿佛失去自我
senses.example: The violin solo ravished the whole audience.
senses.exampleCN: 那一段小提琴独奏让全场听众如痴如醉。
senses.why: The Latin root rapere means to snatch away, so to ravish is to have ones senses and attention carried off by pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 词根 rapere 意为「猛然抓走」，所以 ravish 就是让人的感官与注意力在快乐中被人夺走。

senses.title: To charm visually
senses.titleCN: 使惊艳；美得令人移不开眼
senses.definition: to be so beautiful or impressive that it holds the eye and the mind
senses.definitionCN: 美或壮观到让人双眼与心思都被它吸住
senses.example: The palace gardens ravish every visitor who walks through them.
senses.exampleCN: 走过宫殿花园的每一位访客都会被那里的美景迷住。
senses.why: The eyes are seized by what they see, so the same seizing image slides from delight in general to delight at sight.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛被所看到的东西抓住，于是同一个「被掳」的意象从泛泛的快乐滑向视觉上的惊艳。

senses.title: To carry off by force
senses.definition: to seize and carry away someone or something by force, in an older and now rare use
senses.definitionCN: 用武力劫走或夺走某人某物，此为较旧、现已少见的用法
senses.example: In the old chronicle, raiders ravished the village and its stores.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧编年史里，劫掠者洗劫了村庄和村里的储备。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal sense: rapere means to snatch away by force, with no delight in sight.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面义：rapere 本义就是用力夺走，与快乐无关。

senses.title: Adjective form for beauty
senses.titleCN: 迷人的；美得惊人的（作形容词）
senses.definition: the participle ravishing used to describe someone or something of striking beauty
senses.definitionCN: 分词形式 ravishing 用作形容词，形容极其美丽的某人或某物
senses.example: She looked ravishing in the simple white dress.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着那条简单的白裙子，看上去美得惊人。
senses.why: Pleasure that snatches the eye becomes a settled description: ravishing is now read as a plain adjective of beauty.
senses.whyCN: 抓住眼睛的快乐凝固成固定评价：ravishing 现在就是一个表示美丽的普通形容词。

senses.title: Ecstatic state of the soul
senses.titleCN: 狂喜；神魂颠倒（宗教语境）
senses.definition: a state of holy transport in which the soul is said to be carried beyond itself
senses.definitionCN: 宗教语境中灵魂被带离自身的出神状态
senses.example: The old hymn speaks of a soul ravished by holy love.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古老的赞美诗讲到一颗被神圣之爱摄住的灵魂。
senses.why: Religious writers took the seizing image for the soul being lifted out of the body by divine love.
senses.whyCN: 宗教作者借用了「被掳走」的意象，指灵魂被神圣之爱提出身体之外。

intro.en: Ravish comes from Old French ravir, from Latin rapere, to seize and carry off, with the English verb ending -ish common to verbs borrowed through French.
intro.cn: ravish 来自古法语 ravir，源头是拉丁语 rapere（抓住并带走），动词词尾 -ish 是经法语借入的英语动词常见形式。

items.en: Rapere means to seize, snatch, or carry off by force.
items.cn: rapere 意为抓住、猛夺或强行带走。

items.en: The strengthened form rapire is recorded and probably underlies the later Romance verbs.
items.cn: 一般认为存在加强形式 rapire，后来的罗曼语动词多由此而来。

items.en: Ravir means to seize, snatch away, and later to transport with joy.
items.cn: ravir 意为夺取、掳走，后来也指使人欣喜若狂。

items.en: Ravish enters English with the sense of seizing by force, often in accounts of war.
items.cn: ravish 在十三世纪进入英语，最初表示武力夺取，常用于战争叙述。

items.en: The sense of filling with delight or enchantment becomes common in poetry.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，「使陶醉、使着迷」的含义在诗歌中流行起来。

items.en: The violent sense fades, and the adjective ravishing survives as the everyday form.
items.cn: 暴力的含义逐渐淡去，而形容词 ravishing 成为日常用法而保留下来。

note.en: Ravish belongs with capture, rapture, and rapid through the Latin root rapere, and stands near overwhelm and enchant in meaning.
note.cn: ravish 借拉丁词根 rapere 与 capture、rapture、rapid 同宗，在意义上则与 overwhelm、enchant 相邻。

entries.definition: a feeling of intense pleasure
entries.definitionCN: 狂喜；极度的喜悦，与 ravish 同出拉丁语 rapere

entries.definition: to catch and hold
entries.definitionCN: 捕获；抓住，词根同为 capere 一系的 rapere

entries.definition: moving quickly
entries.definitionCN: 迅速的；急速的，与 ravish 同源自「猛拉带走」

entries.definition: to fill with delight and wonder
to give great pleasure
to affect someone very strongly
entries.definitionCN: 使不知所措；使深受震撼

normalIntro.en: Ravish is the delight that takes you by force: the same root that gives capture and rapture.
normalIntro.cn: ravish 是一种「把人掳走」的快乐：它和 capture、rapture 共用一个词根。

normal.en: Ravish and rapture share the Latin root rapere, to snatch away.
normal.cn: ravish 与 rapture 共拉丁词根 rapere，意为猛夺、掳走。

normal.en: The adjective ravishing is the common modern form, as in a ravishing view.
normal.cn: 形容词 ravishing 是现代常见形式，如「令人惊艳的风景」。

normal.en: Ravished with delight means carried away by joy.
normal.cn: ravished with delight 表示被喜悦冲得神魂颠倒。

normal.en: Compare ravenous: both come from the idea of seizing greedily.
normal.cn: 对比 ravenous：两者都源于「贪婪夺取」的想法。

normal.en: In formal writing, ravish is often replaced by enchant or thrill.
normal.cn: 正式写作中，ravish 常被 enchant 或 thrill 替代。

abstract.en: Picture a hand snatching a flower from the air, leaving the garden breathless.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在空中一把摘走花朵，整座花园都为之屏息。

abstract.en: Imagine a viewer at a gallery stopped mid-step by one painting.
abstract.cn: 想象一位观众在画廊里被一幅画定住，脚步停在半途。

abstract.en: Think of a crowd that forgets the time as the music keeps rising.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被越来越高的乐声包围，完全忘了时间。

examples.en: The sunset over the lake ravished every photographer on the bridge.
examples.cn: 湖面上的晚霞让桥上的每位摄影者都如痴如醉。

examples.en: She wore a ravishing red coat to the winter ball.
examples.cn: 她穿了一件美得惊人的红色大衣去参加冬夜舞会。

examples.en: The soprano ravished her listeners with a single long note.
examples.cn: 女高音用一句长长的音把听众全都迷住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉卫士」——卫兵一把把人「拉」走，人还没反应过来就被拽走了；联想「被猛力拽走后陷入恍惚」。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 rapere（抓住、猛夺、带走）→ 俗拉丁语 rapire → 古法语 ravir → 英语 ravish，核心义「被猛然抓走」。

sensesIntro.en: Ravish moves from delight that carries the mind away, to delight at sight, to the old literal seizing, and then to its adjective and religious forms.
sensesIntro.cn: ravish 从「把心思带走的快乐」出发，扩展到视觉上的惊艳，再回溯古老的「夺取」本义，最后是形容词与宗教用法的延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone standing still because beauty has seized them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人被美猛地抓住，愣在原地。

branches.en: Delight that carries the mind away is the modern core sense.
branches.cn: 把心思带走的快乐是现代核心义项。

branches.en: Beauty that holds the eye is delight at sight.
branches.cn: 抓住双眼的美是视觉上的陶醉。

branches.en: Seizing by force is the oldest literal layer.
branches.cn: 武力夺取是最古老的字面义层。

branches.en: The participle has settled into a plain adjective of beauty.
branches.cn: 分词形式已固化为表示美丽的普通形容词。

branches.en: Both force and holy love take a person out of the ordinary state.
branches.cn: 武力与神圣之爱都把人带离平常状态。

intro.en: Ravish builds a small family in English: ravishing, ravishment, ravisher, all from the same seizing root.
intro.cn: ravish 在英语里构成一小组词族：ravishing、ravishment、ravisher，都出自「夺取」这一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin rapere, to seize, gives ravish along with capture, rapture, and rapid.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rapere（抓住）给出 ravish，也给出 capture、rapture 与 rapid。

items.example: Rapere supplies the snatching image behind ravish.
items.exampleCN: rapere 提供了 ravish 背后的「猛夺」意象。

items.example: Old French ravir is the direct route into English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 ravir 是进入英语的直接路径。

items.example: The ending -ish turns Old French rav into ravish.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ish 把古法语 rav 变成 ravish。

items.example: Ravish keeps both the violent and the delightful senses.
items.exampleCN: ravish 兼有暴力与愉悦两种含义。

items.meaningCN: 构成分词与形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms ravishing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 ravishing。

items.example: Ravishing is now the most used member of the family.
items.exampleCN: ravishing 现在是这个词族中用得最多的形式。

items.meaning: forming nouns of action or state
items.meaningCN: 构成动作或状态名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ment forms ravishment.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ment 构成 ravishment。

items.meaning: a state of ecstasy or raiding
items.example: Ravishment names the state and the old raiding act.
items.exampleCN: ravishment 既指状态，也指古老的劫掠行为。

items.example: The suffix -er forms ravisher, a seizer.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 ravisher，指强夺者。

items.example: Capture shares the root rapere with ravish.
items.exampleCN: capture 与 ravish 共用词根 rapere。

items.example: Rapture and ravish sit on the same Latin base.
items.exampleCN: rapture 与 ravish 处在同一个拉丁语言基础之上。

definition_zh: 试剂；试药
definition_en: a substance that is added to another substance to produce a chemical reaction or to test for something
core_image: 试管里滴入一滴透明液体，整杯溶液立刻变了颜色
scene: 学生把几滴碘液滴进马铃薯切片，颜色慢慢变成深蓝。The student added a few drops of iodine reagent and watched the potato slice turn dark blue.
sceneCN: 这里 reagent 是「试剂」（第 1 个义项：加入另一种物质中引起反应或用于检验的物质）；句意：学生滴入几滴碘试剂，看着马铃薯片变成深蓝色。

derivatives.zh: 由 reagent 加 -less 构成的形容词，义为「不使用试剂的」
由 reagent 与 grade 构成的复合形容词，指「达到试剂纯度的」
与 reagent 同出拉丁语 agere 一系，义为「反应；起化学作用」
react 的名词形式，义为「反应」；试剂正是促成反应的物质

senses.title: A substance used in a reaction
senses.definition: a chemical substance that takes part in a reaction, especially one added to another substance
senses.definitionCN: 参与化学反应的物质，尤指加入另一种物质中的那一种
senses.example: Sulfur dioxide acts as a reagent in this synthesis.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个合成过程中，二氧化硫起试剂的作用。
senses.why: The Latin prefix re- means back, and agere means to act, so a reagent is something that acts back in a process.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语前缀 re- 表示「回、反」，agere 表示「做」，所以试剂是「反过来施加作用」的东西。

senses.title: A substance used for testing
senses.definition: a substance whose colour change or other visible effect shows whether a particular substance is present
senses.definitionCN: 通过变色或其他可见效果显示某种物质是否存在的物质
senses.example: Litmus is a classic reagent for telling acids from bases.
senses.exampleCN: 石蕊是区分酸与碱的经典试剂。
senses.why: A reagent can act back on the sample as a question, and its visible change is the answer.
senses.whyCN: 试剂可以反过来对样品「发问」，而它显示出的变化就是答案。

senses.title: Laboratory stock substance
senses.definition: a bottle or supply of such a substance kept in a laboratory for repeated use
senses.definitionCN: 实验室中为反复使用而储备的此类物质，或盛装它们的瓶子
senses.example: Keep the reagent in a cool cupboard away from sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 把试剂存放在阴凉、避光的橱柜里。
senses.why: Once substances are named reagents, the stock on the shelf is also called by that name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这类物质被叫作试剂，货架上那一瓶瓶储备也就沿用了这个名称。

senses.title: The restricting partner
senses.titleCN: 限量试剂；限制产量的那一方
senses.definition: the reagent that is used up first and therefore limits how much product can form
senses.definitionCN: 最先被用完、因而限制产物产量的那一种试剂
senses.example: Oxygen is the limiting reagent in that combustion test.
senses.exampleCN: 在那次燃烧实验中，氧气是限量试剂。
senses.why: In a reaction every partner is a reagent, so chemists name the one that acts back on the whole yield.
senses.whyCN: 反应中每一种反应物都可算试剂，化学家于是用它来指那个决定整体产量的。

senses.title: Figurative use for a stirrer
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：激起反应的东西
senses.definition: something that is added in order to provoke a visible response or change
senses.definitionCN: 为了让可见的反应或变化发生而加入的东西
senses.example: Her quiet question was a reagent that set the whole room arguing.
senses.exampleCN: 她那句轻轻的提问像一个试剂，让满屋子的人争辩起来。
senses.why: The chemical image moves easily to any setting where one small addition makes a large visible effect.
senses.whyCN: 化学意象很容易移植到任何「加入一点点就引发大变化」的场合。

intro.en: Reagent is a scientific coinage built in English from the Latin prefix re- and the root of agere, to act; it names the substance that acts back in a reaction.
intro.cn: reagent 是英语里的科学新造词，由拉丁语前缀 re- 与 agere（做、起作用）的词根构成，指在反应中「反过来施加作用」的物质。

items.en: Agere means to act, do, or drive.
items.cn: agere 意为做、行动、驱赶。

items.en: Agens, agentis is the present participle, one who acts.
items.cn: agens（属格 agentis）是现在分词，指「行动者」。

items.en: The prefix re- adds the idea of back or in return.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 添加了「回、反向」的意思。

items.en: Reagent appears in English in chemistry, naming a substance that reacts on another.
items.cn: reagent 在十七世纪出现在英语化学文献中，指对另一种物质起作用的物质。

items.en: In modern chemistry it covers reactants, test substances, and limiting partners in a reaction.
items.cn: 在现代化学中，它涵盖反应物、检验用物质以及反应中的限量一方。

note.en: Reagent is easily confused with agency and urgent by spelling, and stands near reactant, solution, and catalyst in laboratory speech.
note.cn: reagent 在拼写上容易与 agency、urgent 混淆；在实验室用语中则与 reactant、solution、catalyst 同场出现。

entries.definition: the ability or power to act
entries.definitionCN: 能动性；代理机构，与 reagent 共有 agent 词形但意义不同

entries.definition: needing quick action
entries.definitionCN: 紧急的；急迫的，只是发音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: something that produces an effect
entries.definitionCN: 作用物；媒介，与 reagent 同出拉丁语 agere

entries.definition: a substance that is changed in a chemical reaction
entries.definitionCN: 反应物（在化学反应中被消耗、被改变的物质）

entries.definition: a substance that speeds a reaction without being used up
entries.definitionCN: 催化剂（加速反应而自身不被消耗）

entries.definition: a liquid with a substance dissolved in it
entries.definitionCN: 溶液（溶解有某种物质的液体）

normalIntro.en: Reagent is the agent that acts back: the Latin prefix re- plus agent, the substance that works on another one.
normalIntro.cn: reagent 是「反过来起作用的 agent」：re- 加上 agent，就是作用于另一种物质的物质。

normal.en: Break it as re- plus agent: an agent that acts back on a sample.
normal.cn: 拆成 re- 加 agent：对样品「反向」起作用的媒介。

normal.en: A limiting reagent runs out first and limits the product.
normal.cn: 限量试剂最先用完，从而限制产物的量。

normal.en: A reagent bottle sits on the lab shelf for repeated use.
normal.cn: 试剂瓶放在实验室架子上，供反复使用。

normal.en: Add a reagent and watch for a colour change.
normal.cn: 加入一种试剂，然后观察颜色变化。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with reactant: a reactant is used up, a reagent is often the added one.
normal.cn: 别与 reactant 混淆：反应物会被消耗掉，试剂常指加入的那一种。

abstract.en: Picture one clear drop falling into a beaker and turning it bright pink.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴透明液体落入烧杯，整杯立刻变成亮粉色。

abstract.en: Imagine a tiny litmus strip on a wet table turning from blue to red.
abstract.cn: 想象一张小小的石蕊试纸沾了湿痕，由蓝转红。

abstract.en: See a row of identical bottles on a shelf, each with a white label.
abstract.cn: 看见架子上一排一模一样的瓶子，每个都贴着白标签。

examples.en: The enzyme is a biological reagent that speeds up the breakdown of starch.
examples.cn: 这种酶是一种生物试剂，能加快淀粉的分解。

examples.en: Never return unused reagents to their original bottles.
examples.cn: 千万不要把没用完的试剂倒回原来的瓶子。

examples.en: The test uses a simple reagent to show whether copper is present.
examples.cn: 这项检测用一种简单试剂来表明是否存在铜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞进特」——一滴「瑞」剂「进」入试管，反应「特」别快；再记它的结构：试剂就是专门「反向作用」的 agent。这只是谐音与拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语前缀 re-（回、反向）+ agere（做、起作用）→ agent（作用者）→ 英语 reagent，指在反应中对另一种物质起作用的物质。

sensesIntro.en: Reagent starts as any substance that acts in a reaction, narrows to the substance added for testing, and then extends to laboratory stock, to the limiting partner, and to a figurative stirrer.
sensesIntro.cn: reagent 先指任何在反应中起作用的物质，再收窄为用于检验时加入的物质，随后扩展为实验室储备、限量一方以及比喻意义上的「引发者」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one drop changes the whole beaker.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴试剂改变整杯溶液。

branches.en: A substance that acts in a reaction is the core sense.
branches.cn: 在反应中起作用的物质是核心义项。

branches.en: The testing sense makes the visible change into an answer.
branches.cn: 检验义把可见变化变成答案。

branches.en: The stored bottle on the shelf inherits the name.
branches.cn: 架子上的储备瓶沿用了这个名称。

branches.en: The limiting partner is the reaction sense pointed at yield.
branches.cn: 限量一方是反应义项指向产量的用法。

branches.en: Both a test reagent and a figurative reagent provoke a response.
branches.cn: 检验试剂与比喻意义上的试剂都会激起反应。

intro.en: Reagent is a compound of the prefix re- and the Latin agent, and it sits with react, reaction, and agent in English.
intro.cn: reagent 由前缀 re- 与拉丁语 agent 组合而成，在英语里与 react、reaction、agent 同族。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere, to act, gives agens and agentis, which English uses for agent, reagent, and react.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere（做）给出 agens 与 agentis，英语由此构成 agent、reagent、react。

items.example: The prefix re- adds a turning back in reagent.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 在 reagent 中加入「反向」的意味。

items.example: Agere is the root of a large English family.
items.exampleCN: agere 是一个庞大英语词族的根源。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词与名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ent turns the stem into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 把词干变成名词。

items.example: Agent is the base that reagent extends.
items.exampleCN: agent 是 reagent 扩展的基础。

items.meaning: a substance used in a reaction
items.example: Reagent names the substance that reacts on another.
items.exampleCN: reagent 指对另一种物质起作用的物质。

items.example: React keeps the same acting root.
items.exampleCN: react 保留同一个「作用」词根。

items.example: Reaction comes through French from the same root.
items.exampleCN: reaction 经法语从同一词根而来。

items.example: The suffix -less forms reagentless.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -less 构成 reagentless。

items.meaningCN: 表示某个品质等级的构词成分
items.example: The form -grade forms reagent-grade.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -grade 构成 reagent-grade。

items.example: Agenda also descends from agere, things to be done.
items.exampleCN: agenda 同样出自 agere，意为「要做的事」。
